News.title: We live in UK’s parking fine capital – council has fleeced us of £2million so now we’re taping over our number plates
News.content:
CASH COW We live in UK’s parking fine capital – council has fleeced us of £2million so now we’re taping over our number plates

FURIOUS locals have started taping over their number plates in the traffic fine capital of the UK after council officials raked in more than £2million from one street.

London’s Barking Council dished out a staggering 33,440 penalty notices in the last financial year to drivers stung by restrictions on Station Parade.



Only buses, taxis and emergency service vehicles have been allowed on the road since the council changed the rules in 2021 – but many motorists are still being caught out.

Angry locals claim the changes have not been communicated clearly, signs are unclear and traffic wardens are behaving like “hawks”.



Michael Goldson, a delivery driver for pharmacists on the street, told The Sun: “It’s a disaster. I know people who don’t want to do this route because each side they get tickets. But we have to deliver to the pharmacies.”

Under the changes, delivery drivers are not allowed along Station Parade and must approach shops from Cambridge Road rather than Longbridge Road.

But Goldson, who moved to the UK from Jamaica in 1994, says he racked up four fines in one week because he had no idea.

He also says there are time restrictions on delivery drivers in the area that are not made clear enough.



The Sun could only find one sign with guidance on times for delivery drivers tucked away on a small path behind the high street.

There were no signs offering guidance for delivery drivers on the Cambridge Road approach to the shops.

Goldson added: “After 6am to 10.30am, and then 5pm to 7pm, there is a camera that picks us up.



“I supply pharmacies in the town centre but it is a problem everywhere. I will do two trips in the afternoon.”

On the high street a different van even had his number plate covered in black tape.

A local grocer, Nurettin Erdogan, who is opening a new shop, insists the time windows for delivery drivers are not enough for local businesses.



He told The Sun: “This time is not enough and it needs to be longer.

“I have been fined outside these hours and everybody says it is not long enough.

“I see it a lot. There is a huge problem with deliveries, lorries don’t have the space.”

Another motorist, Dimo Stoyanov, says he was hit by an astonishing 11 fines in just a matter of days.



The HR advisor had been using his usual Vicarage Road car park and had no idea about a new rule that allowed drivers to access it from Cambridge Road but not the other direction, and vice versa.

He told The Sun: “I was parking there for more than a year in around 2021 and I would always use it for work.

“Sometimes I would turn left and sometimes I would turn right when I entered the street.

“For one year I never got a penalty so it was very natural to keep going either way. Then one day I received two penalty notices saying that I had entered a street restricted for cars.



“But they took about two weeks to send me the penalty. I thought that means, from that day, every time I turned right from Vicarage Field car park to Station Parade I got a penalty.

“Then I went back to check and I could see new signs but for one year I’d been driving and it comes very naturally, so I wasn’t looking for new signs.

“I saw one person spend an entire day warning other drivers on the road because one after another, hundreds of cars were driving into the road and this guy was like ‘stop, stop there is a camera!’



“I was a student back then so I didn’t have enough money and I just explained the situation, that I had been driving in that street for more than one year and I had no idea there were new signs or cameras.

“I asked them to cancel the penalties and I said I just don’t have the money to pay this. I think they were around £65 if I paid within two weeks, but if I don’t they would be £130.”

Thankfully for Stoyanov, who has lived in Barking for seven years, the council cancelled – but he questions how many others didn’t have the same luck or didn’t think to challenge it.



He added: “They cancelled and I think I was very lucky. They didn’t give a reason for cancelling other than on this occasion, they were cancelling.

“I apologised and promised never to do it again, saying that after parking routinely for more than one year you don’t just look for new signs.

“But after seeing people continuing to drive through the street even though there are signs, I assumed people were not aware of the changes.

“The sign was also really tiny and on top of other, different signs. It was not easy to spot.”



Locals also pointed the finger at overzealous traffic wardens they say are too eager to fine.

One tradesman, who asked to stay anonymous, told us: “One of the main issues around this Barking area is that the road is quite congested.

“Sometimes during rush hour with more vehicle congestion, it makes it very difficult for you to manoeuvre your vehicle in certain areas.

“But the other issue is with parking: unless you have a permit it is difficult to find parking.



“A lot of these bays are disabled bays but the wardens around the area are like hawks, the minute they see a vehicle in violation, they instantly issue a ticket for it.

“It is quite a shame because at the same time this area is quite a deprived area so the income for a lot of people is not necessarily high.

“A lot of people coming out, like Uber drivers and stuff, drop off passengers and I know they are allowed a settling down time but it’s how tolerant the parking attendant is at the time.

“Some are okay while others are really sort of targeted.

“Sometimes it appears they are commission based because of how eager they are to issue tickets.



“I was done further down the high street. There is a sign there saying no permitted vehicles but the sign is so high up it’s not a clear visual spot.

“I was done there just for taking a wrong turn. And funnily enough my navigation sent me down that road.

“I took a wrong turn, but only until you’ve taken the wrong turn do you realise. There needs to be a grace period.”



Narcis Vlasleanu, a van driver, said: “There needs to be a bigger signal for attention and the times need to be clear.

“This makes money for the council. It does not help the people.”

The council said at the time the plans were introduced to reduce traffic and create a safer space for thousands passing through the area.

It cited 23 reported collisions and 26 casualties between 2014 and 2018, with the majority hurt being pedestrians.

It insists consultation with locals followed an 18-month trial period.



All business owners were consulted and sent leaflets outlining the changes, it added, and said the number of passengers passing through Barking Station had doubled in the past decade with 14.5million journeys every year.

A spokesperson for Barking Council said: “All on street signage is compliant with the Traffic Signs Regulations and General Directions Act 2016…”

“Drivers must enter Longbridge Road by taking a right turn from Salisbury Avenue, they cannot take a left turn as traffic in Station Parade is prohibited on a 24 hour basis…

“Drivers must enter Longbridge Road by taking a right turn from Salisbury Avenue, they cannot take a left turn as traffic in Station Parade is prohibited on a 24 hour basis…

“There are loading bays on Salisbury Avenue, Clockhouse, and on Station Parade near the station before the restrictions start.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Asked how motorists using taped over number plates is being policed, they said: “If the vehicle is travelling on street we cannot action at this time but would inform the police if we later see the vehicle on street.”

They added: “The Council can only issue a penalty charge notice to offending vehicles, the volume of penalties issued is relative to the motorists who are not compliant with the regulations.”

News.title: Shock pictures show ‘snipers with air rifles taking out over 600 pigeons in London Tube culls’
News.content:
'CULLING' HORROR Shock pictures show ‘snipers with air rifles taking out over 600 pigeons in London Tube culls’

SHOCKING pictures appear to show snipers aiming air rifles at train stations – with Transport for London workers accused of killing over 650 pigeons in a mass cull.

TfL is said to have organised at least 123 shoots between March 2024 and March 2026 in an effort to rid stations of birds nesting on ledges or trapped behind netting, according to Manchester Pigeon Rehab (MPR).



TfL is adamant its approach is “focused on prevention” and that the “avoidance of animal cruelty is taken very seriously”.

However, “in a few small number of cases” – when such measures aren’t successful, the removal of pigeons and nests “is undertaken with consideration” and as a “last resort”.



Shocking pictures appear to show TfL workers clad in hi-vis aiming air rifles at birds and in one image, allegedly taken at Stanmore Station, a man appears to have his boot clamped on a bleeding pigeon.

Over the two years, MPR claims 655 pigeons were shot, 17 active nests were removed and at least seven chicks were killed or removed.

Some baby chicks and fledglings were left without parents or their necks were snapped using “humane bird dispatchers”, the group says.

The methods have been met with some backlash and campaigners have filed a crime report to the British Transport Police as they say the birds suffered unnecessarily.

The data was collated by MPR who claimed TfL did not explore non-lethal options or take reasonable steps to mitigate pigeon suffering.

They claim the culling took place after hours, typically between midnight and 5am.



The FoI requests found that the shootings were contracted out to AGS one and were performed under a GL41 licence.

The licence reportedly has several conditions, including taking reasonable measures to minimise suffering.

Natural England advises “avoiding lethal control” during breeding season.



A spokesperson for Manchester Pigeon Rehab added: “Pigeons are intelligent and highly social animals.

“They are capable of forming long term bonds, share the responsibility of raising young, and can solve complex problems.

“Modern feral pigeons descended from birds that were once domesticated by humans where they carried our messages and fought in our wars.

“Pigeons are intelligent and highly social animals. They are capable of forming long term bonds, share the responsibility of raising young, and can solve complex problems.

“We believe Transport for London should immediately end lethal control in favour of habitat modification, humane deterrents and other non-lethal management measures.



“In some circumstances this may also mean accepting that wildlife will continue to exist in shared urban spaces.”

A spokesperson for Transport for London said: “Our approach is focused on prevention, and the avoidance of animal cruelty is taken very seriously.

“We continue to invest in preventative measures as our primary approach, exhausting all appropriate non-lethal methods, and have significantly increased our mitigations on stations and in depots as part of this work.

“Unfortunately, in a few small number of cases, preventative measures are not always successful or effective, creating an unsafe environment.

“When this is the case, we work with our suppliers to ensure that the removal of pigeons, or their nests, is undertaken with consideration and only ever as a last resort when other deterrents have failed.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Ultimately, we have a duty of care to customers, staff, contractors and other third parties to maintain a safe, clean environment for those using or working on our property.

“Pigeon waste carries risks of bacteria and insects, while nesting and waste material creates fire hazards and structural damage.”

News.title: Zookeeper famous for kissing bears has arm ripped off by beast years after losing leg in another attack
News.content:
GRIZZLY HORROR Zookeeper famous for kissing bears has arm ripped off by beast years after losing leg in another attack

A ZOOKEEPER famous for kissing bears is fighting for her life after a captive grizzly tore her arm clean off – following a similar attack where she lost her leg.

Vera Blishch, 62, is in critical condition in Russia after a routine bear feeding exercise cost her a second limb to the jaws of the animal.



The horrifying incident occurred when Blishch was feeding a Himalayan black bear at the Dora Park zoo in Ussuriysk.

The animal tragically tore her arm off.



Blishch was found unconscious after the attack.

It is understood the trainer had raised the bear from a cub.



This is not the first time Blishch has been involved in a bear attack.

Six years ago, she lost a leg and a finger in another bear mauling.

Despite the most recent ordeal, she pleaded from her hospital bed that the Himalayan black bear should not be put down.



Taking the entirety of blame, she said: “There is definitely no guilt to the animal.”

Blishch famed in Russia for being fearless with the carnivorous animals and has worked with them for more than 30 years.

She gained status as a conservationist, highly regarded for her campaign to save animals that were impacted by severe flooding in the far east of Russia in 2015.

She said: “Even by just kissing the bear now I might lose my head within a split second.

“To work with a bear, you must have a special feeling. We say it’s a feeling sent by God.



“It’s very dangerous to do this.”

Dave Garsheli, an international bear conservation expert told The Sun: “Normally, captive bears are less dangerous because they have become habituated to people.

“Normally, if one raises a bear as a cub, it would be quite tame, and get attached to the person, almost akin to a dog.

“But something must have gone awry in this case.”

News.title: I was dragged off street at 13 & raped on filthy mattress by Asian grooming gang for years…cops accused ME of blackmail
News.content:
ELLIE Reynolds, 13, was walking along the street when a car pulled up in front of her. Out stepped a man she recognised. He was in a relationship with someone she knew and ran the local Indian takeaway. Everyone called him Sarj.

“Shock and fear hit me as, before I really realised what was happening, I was dragged into the back of the car,” she says.



“I was plied with drugs and taken to a top floor flat. You don’t know what’s going on. You’re out of your head. There were these dirty mattresses on the floor and you’re in that room and you do as you’re told. It was a multiple gang rape of a child.”

There followed, what she described as five years of hell as she was gang raped, beaten and tortured by her abusers. Her parents were alarmed by her change in behaviour, her secrecy about where she was going and her weight loss. But she was too frightened of reprisals if she told them or anyone else what was happening.

When Ellie eventually summoned the courage to tell police, she was shocked to find that instead of arresting her abusers, they arrested her instead.



Now in the three-part Sky documentary Barrow: The Truth Behind the Grooming Lie, Ellie and other women from the Cumbrian town of Barrow-in-Furness talk about their horrific experiences at the hands of gangs of Asian men who groomed and abused them for years.

It begins with the notorious case of a fellow Ellie in the town, Ellie Williams, who made a series of lurid claims in 2020 about being raped and beaten by a grooming gang, posting online images of her bruised and cut body.

There had already been a public outcry following the exposure of the grooming of young white girls by Asian gangs in Derby, Rotherham, Greater Manchester, Rochdale, Oxford and Telford. Police and authorities were accused of a lack of action due to sensitivity of ethnicity and fears of being branded racist or inciting their communities.

Now, determined to crack down, they took Williams’s claims very seriously until she was sensationally exposed as a serial fantasist who lied, fabricated evidence and self-injured herself to frame innocent men. In January 2023 she was sentenced to eight and a half years in prison for perverting the course of justice.

Despite this, Williams’s mum Allison and elder sister, Lucy, who give first-time interviews in the documentary, believe that her lies masked some truth.



“I’ve always said that I know Ellie [Williams] has told some lies,” says Allison. “However, she hasn’t lied about it all. There’s truth in some of what she is saying.”

But her proven lies and conviction were a blow to vulnerable and abused young girls everywhere who now worried about whether their accusations would be believed. Like Ellie Reynolds.

Cumbrian Police were quick to make a statement that there was no evidence of grooming by Asian gangs in Barrow. But several local women were appalled. They knew it was occurring because they had seen or experienced it themselves.



Did the focus on proving one young woman a liar lead to denial of a wider grooming problem?

Linking many of the women’s stories is Shah Joman Miah, known as Sarj who, along with his two brothers, Jai and Ali, ran the Indian takeaway, Iesha’s. Sarj had been named by Williams as one of her abusers and she had his name in her phone. Twenty months after she was jailed, he was convicted on multiple accounts of sexual abuse, including the rape of young girls.

“Grooming is often thought to be older men plying girls with free drinks and drugs and them thinking they are their boyfriends,” says Ellie Reynolds. “But it’s not always like that. You can have an experience like I did where I was taken off the street in 2014 and then it was five years of hell.

“There were three men who operated in a gang. They were drugging, torturing and raping me. They got gratification out of scaring me. There’s absolutely nothing that these guys wouldn’t do to put the living fear into you.”

When Ellie’s dad, Ian Piper, got a tip-off from a young man as to where his daughter was – a dirty flat in a place called Egerton Court – he informed a police officer, who knocked on the door. Ellie answered.



“When you are around multiple men who work for your main abuser, you know that you can’t talk, so I gave him a false name,” she says. “He replied, ‘That’s not who you are though, is it, Ellie?’”

He brought her out with a frightened Ellie screaming at him.

“I was overwhelmed with anger, shouting, ‘Now look what you’ve done’ and I pushed him and was arrested for assaulting a police officer.



“They considered me to be a troubled teenager. They didn’t look into why I was in a flat with three grown men. I was never asked ‘Are you okay? Are you safe? Is there anything we should know about?’”

In 2018, when she was 17, she told police everything that had happened to her by her abusers.

“Less than 24 hours after reporting a gang rape, the police arrived at our house and I was arrested for blackmail.”

Just hours before she had reported her abuse, a young man had alleged she had blackmailed him for money by text for relatively small amounts totalling £275. Ellie explained to police that she had been forced to send those messages by her abusers and that she believed he had explicit sexual images of her.

A week later, police arrested Sarj and two other men she accused. All three were later released on bail pending further investigation.



Sarj had been named by both Ellies as their main abuser. Ruth (not her real name) was the third to report him to police in August 2018, saying she had been in a relationship with him since she was 13 and he was in his 20s.

“We met at a bonfire party in 2008,” says Ruth. He seemed so nice and we kept in touch before meeting up again. He used to pick me up from school and we went on drives. It felt exciting. He used to buy me everything – phone, top-ups, beer, fags, hair extensions – anything I wanted. He’d say how much he loved me and I used to think it was romantic.”

Ruth and other girls, such as “Laura”, loved hanging out with Sarj, Jai and Ali and other older men – in the back of the takeaway, after it closed. Here, they enjoyed drink, drugs and music and felt like they were being treated like grown-ups.

Laura, who was in a relationship with 31-year-old Ali when she was 15, says, “We all thought we were good friends dating men who were brothers. But one night, Ali, Sarj and Jai went outside for a chat. Then Jai came back in and said to me, ‘You know you want me. Nobody needs to find out.’



“He gripped the back of my shorts and pulled them down. I kept saying no, leave me alone, but he pinned me down. I don’t know how long it went on for. It felt like a long time. I felt sick. I walked back to my grandad’s and I used bleach to scrub myself because I was that disgusted.”

Elizabeth Speirs, whose partner worked at the takeaway, says she saw young girls in school uniforms coming in every day to hang out with men from Barrow, Leeds and Bolton.



“There were always underage girls there,” says Elizabeth. “I must have seen at least 40, 50 girls in and out at different times.”

It wasn’t long before Ruth saw the darker side of her “boyfriend.”

“I thought I loved Sarj and then he just started getting controlling,” she says. “He didn’t want me going out with my friends. He had a temper and was scary when he wanted to be, screaming and shouting in my face and pushing me around. Afterwards, he’d be sorry and buy me something and say he wouldn’t do it again, but it kept happening.”

When Ruth became pregnant at 16, she decided that she did not want to be around Sarj any more.

“He didn’t give up easily,” she says. “He posted a dead rat through my letterbox once.”



When Laura ended her relationship with Ali and reported him to police, she says he told her, “Keep your mouth shut. You know what I’m capable of. I will set your house on fire, rape you again, batter you.”

But despite her bravery in speaking out the CPS decided there was insufficient evidence to provide a prospect of conviction. Ellie Reynolds also got such a letter in 2019 which added: “Had I charged the suspect in this matter, the defence would have suggested to the jury that you had made this reported rape in an attempt to excuse your criminality in the commission of blackmail.”

“It felt degrading and demoralising, just not being believed,” she says. “My theory is that they didn’t want the truth to come out about Barrow, that there were actually grooming gangs in Barrow. They wanted me to be silenced.”

In October 2024 the Miah brothers, charged with 62 counts of child sexual abuse between 1996 and 2010 in Barrow and Leeds, were found guilty.

During the trial it emerged that they had much younger victims who were of the same ethnicity as them. The youngest was seven.



Sarj, 38 and Jai, 48, were given life sentences. Ali, 47 was sentenced to 14 years.

Elizabeth was amongst those who gave evidence, saying how she had been threatened not to talk to the police.

Ellie Reynolds, who set up a campaign group called Justice for the Girls to help grooming victims, did not have her allegations included in the charges. A year later, she was acquitted of blackmail.



“When I set up Justice for the Girls, I felt like I took my own justice in having a voice,” she says. “You are inclined to think that you are on your own but I wasn’t the only girl at that time. There was a wide range of victims who had also been through it.

“Some of my abusers are still on the streets without any convictions. It’s an open secret now in this area that it wasn’t just three men. There were a lot more.”

Cumbria Constabulary rejects the suggestion that it intended to silence Ellie Reynolds or her family. It said it had a duty to investigate the blackmail complaint because there was an identified victim of blackmail.

It acknowledged shortcomings in the support provide to Laura and Elizabeth in 2010 and said its approach to victims has significantly developed since then. It said both women later received support.

It also acknowledged that victim support practices may not always have met the desired standard when compared to current practice. It says it has strengthened its response through various initiatives and continues to learn from feedback.



Sarj Miah was invited to respond to the allegations made by Ellie Reynolds and Ellie Williams in the documentary but did not reply.

Barrow: The Truth Behind the Grooming Lie. 9pm Sky documentaries, Sunday, 2 August

News.title: Bomb shelter maps hastily slapped up in Moscow & defences urgently bolstered as deadly Ukrainian drones wreak havoc
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

MOSCOW ON ALERT Bomb shelter maps hastily slapped up in Moscow & defences urgently bolstered as deadly Ukrainian drones wreak havoc

BOMB shelter maps have been issued across Moscow after Putin ordered a vast new string of air defences over fears of Ukrainian missiles.

Intelligence analysts have now begun revealing hundreds of emergency refuge sites across the capital’s surrounding districts.



Putin is aiming to turn the country into a defence fortress as fear sweeps across the nation.

Official interactive maps identifying hundreds of emergency shelters have appeared in several districts around the Russian capital.



The extraordinary move comes after residents complained they were left dangerously unprepared during previous Ukrainian strikes.

In the Lyubertsy district, officials published a map on July 30 showing hundreds of so-called “underground spaces” in Lyubertsy, Dzerzhinsky, Oktyabrsky and neighbouring communities.

READ MORE IN WORLD NEWS UNDER SIEGE Please don’t bomb us, beg Russians in plea as Ukraine blitz 'Russia's Amazon'

But the supposed shelters are far from impregnable bunkers.

They include apartment block basements, underground car parks, post offices and other buildings rather than solely purpose-built, blast-resistant shelters.

Podolsk district authorities have also published a map listing every active “temporary shelter point”, complete with its floor area and estimated capacity.

Residents have been told to take only essential possessions, including identity documents, medicines and a mobile phone with its charger.



Similar shelter information has also surfaced in the Odintsovo district.

The frantic preparations come amid chilling warnings that Ukraine could soon have ballistic missiles capable of reaching Moscow.

Denys Shtilerman, an owner of Ukrainian weapons manufacturer Fire Point, has said its new FP-9 ballistic-missile attacks on the Russian capital could begin within weeks once testing is completed.

The missile has a formidable 530-mile range.

Unlike comparatively slow-moving long-range drones, ballistic missiles plunge down at enormous speed, giving air-defence crews precious little time to detect, track and intercept them.



The sudden shelter drive also follows fury over the authorities’ failure to warn residents during a huge Ukrainian drone raid in June.

Residents of Ramenskoye, Kotelniki and Krasnogorsk complained they received no text messages and heard no air-raid sirens.

Many only realised the attack was under way after seeing drones overhead, hearing explosions or witnessing the damage.



Now satellite researchers have uncovered a staggering expansion of Moscow’s defensive shield.

Around two dozen new towers designed to carry Pantsir short-range air-defence systems have been built in a ring roughly 25 miles from central Moscow.

Other positions have been thrown up to shield Putin’s Novo-Ogaryovo official residence, Vnukovo airport and the capital’s oil refinery, which was hit twice in June.

Open-source intelligence researcher Jembob said approximately 24 new Pantsir towers had been constructed around Moscow in just two months.

His analysis identified some 79 towers within 31 miles of the capital, another eight or nine outside that perimeter and around 30 ramp-based positions.



Several Pantsir-SMD systems have also reportedly been stationed on Moscow rooftops.

At least two new sites have meanwhile been created for the powerful long-range S-400 system.

In total, researchers have identified approximately 120 to 125 short-range air-defence positions in and around Moscow.

The defensive surge is a stark sign of Putin’s growing anxiety over Ukraine’s ability to punch through the capital’s supposedly formidable shield.



Russians painted a desperate plea to Ukranian drone pilots to spare their warehouses as Volodymyr Zelensky’s troops continue to blitz Russia’s Amazon equivalent.

Some of the new towers outside the main ring appear to have been positioned specifically to protect vital electrical substations.

Russia has also established an extraordinary belt of air defences around Putin’s secluded Valdai palace, between Moscow and St Petersburg.

Ukrainian monitoring channels claim Kyiv’s sustained campaign is forcing Russia to activate air defences around the capital almost daily and across multiple approaches.



The relentless attacks are giving Russia a taste of the horror it subjects its “enemy”.

Dronebomber+, a Ukrainian monitoring group, plotted approximately 500 reports of air-defence activity or claimed interceptions in the Moscow region during June alone.

The frantic reinforcement programme has also spread to some of Russia’s most important energy sites.

New towers have been built around refineries at Ryazan, Kstovo and Yaroslavl, as well as near Ust-Luga and Vyborg – crucial hubs for Russia’s oil, gas and export infrastructure.

But researchers say the bulk of the sophisticated new towers have appeared around Moscow and northern Russia.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Critical targets in the south, meanwhile, are often protected by cheaper earth ramps.

The stark disparity suggests Putin is concentrating precious air-defence resources around the capital, his personal residences and strategically vital northern facilities.

News.title: ‘Penthouse Pet’ Adva Lavie ‘tears off ankle monitor & steals Rolex watches’ while on bail for ‘robbing sugar daddies’
News.content:
AN LA influencer accused of swindling sugar daddies has been arrested for allegedly stealing Rolexes while out on bail “after ripping off her ankle monitor”.

Adva Lavie was arrested following an investigation into claims she had stolen over $35,000 worth of luxury items as well as a disabled parking pass in Idaho.



Lavie was arrested on Wednesday, July 29, in Beverly Hills on an outstanding felony warrant stemming from an Idaho police investigation.

Lavie already faces several theft-related charges, including residential burglary, in Los Angeles County for which she was on an electronic monitor tag.



When Beverly Hills officers took Lavie into custody, she had removed her electronic ankle monitor, court papers revealed.

Authorities in Riverside County, California, said Lavie, also known as Mia Ventura, allegedly stole from two separate victims at an Airbnb rental on Spiaggia Place in Indio on April 2025.



One instance involved an alleged theft of a $8,600 Rolex, $700 Louis Vuitton sunglasses, an $1,800 Louis Vuitton card holder and the victim’s disabled parking pass, police said.

Surveillance footage from inside the home appeared to show Lavie taking the victim’s property from his Tesla, investigators said.



The victim, who identified himself to NBCLA as Oscar, said he felt “violated”.

It is understood Lavie had been staying at an Airbnb with Oscar during the 2025 Coachella music festival.

He called the police once he noticed the alleged theft.



Another victim in Idaho claims Lavie stole a Rolex watch valued at $25,000 after the two shared a room.

When the luxury watch went missing, the victim suspected Lavie and reported the theft to police.

The Riverside County District Attorney’s Office did not file charges against Lavie due to “insufficient evidence,” according to the Indio Police Department.

Lavie was previously arrested and charged with six felonies for suspected romance-scamming in 2025, to which she pleased not guilty.

Lavie’s bail conditions included not being able to leave California without permission, the stripping away of her passport and the instalment of an ankle monitor.



Prosecutors say between 2023 and 2025 Lavie trawled through online platforms and developed close relationships with wealthy older men.

Police allege she posed as a girlfriend and travel companion to older men to gain access to their homes, before pilfering from her unsuspecting victims.

But before her 2025 arrest, Lavie had already made a name for herself in Hollywood with people warning to look out for her.

Speaking after the recent LA arrest, Oscar said: “We don’t really know how this is going to go, but it’s a step forward that we’ve been waiting for.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Hopefully, she can be brought to justice.”



She will have to appear in Riverside County for the April 2025 grand theft charges after she is set to make a courtroom appearance in LA County on July 31.

News.title: Horrifying moment wildfire ignites next to Ibiza airport runway as panicked Brit tourists fear plane will ‘blow up’
News.content:
THIS is the horrifying moment a raging wildfire erupts just metres from an Ibiza airport runway as terrified Brits feared their plane would “blow up”.

British tourists flying home to London were left fearing the worst after a ferocious blaze suddenly tore through a field beside their plane.



Holidaymakers on a British Airways flight watched in horror as the fast-moving inferno surged dangerously close to the runway.

One passenger told The Sun the entire plane descended into panic as the flames appeared to creep towards the aircraft’s jet fuel.



Marco Schiavo, 30, had been visiting the Spanish island on a business trip when he spotted the terrifying blaze.

He said the plane had already been delayed for two hours because of technical difficulties before it finally began taxiing towards the runway.

He said: “We eventually got on the runway and then we noticed there was a small fire on the field opposite us. So we were literally just sitting there on the runway watching it.

“And then it just rapidly escalated. It was crazy.

“It started as a really small thing and then after about 60 seconds it was nearly halfway through the field.

“It was going through the field really quickly just because it was so hot I think.”



The Sun’s exclusive footage captures a wall of orange flames devouring the parched field directly beside the runway as thick black and grey smoke billows across the landscape.

Spanish authorities declared the blaze an agricultural fire before scrambling a fire engine and two aircraft to battle the inferno.

At least two homes were evacuated and several people were treated for smoke inhalation as the frightening blaze spread.

Mr Schiavo said terrified passengers began raising the alarm with cabin crew as they watched the flames race across the field.



He said: “People were out of their seats, getting up and looking as they realised how fast it was escalating.

“They were starting to panic because we were so close to where it was.

“Obviously we’re an aeroplane so we’ve got jet fuel and it was that close that if any bit of wind came over and it sparked up something the whole plane would blow up.

“There was a couple with a really young baby behind us and they were getting quite panicky.



“Naturally, you just want to get away, people were saying that to the air hostess.

“She hadn’t even realised, we were all looking out the window and she was just on her iPad, but when we told her she was like ‘Oh my God, I’ve got to talk to the captain’.”

The British Airways flight eventually took off safely for London City Airport, but the terrifying blaze triggered severe delays that continued throughout the rest of the day.

The frightening airport drama comes as Spain battles a devastating wildfire crisis after a succession of blistering heatwaves left vegetation tinder-box dry.

More than 116,000 people have been forced to flee their homes this week as raging wildfires rip through parts of the country.



Temperatures are tipped to soar to 40C in Madrid this week, piling fresh misery on exhausted fire crews and holidaymakers heading to Spain.

Seven Brits were among 13 people killed this month after savage wildfires tore through Almeria, including a 93-year-old British woman.

Four British victims were found after their bodies were discovered inside a burnt-out car.

Spain’s government declared a state of emergency as multiple monstrous fires closed in on the capital, threatening to merge and repeatedly forcing residents from their homes.

Civil protection chief Virginia Barcones said this week the country was battling a “monster” in the huge blaze around Avila, a major town 55 miles north-west of Madrid.



She told state broadcaster TVE: “We are dealing with a perimeter of 280 kilometres (173 miles) encompassing 77,000 hectares (190,000 acres).”

The colossal blaze has scorched an area roughly equivalent in size to New York City or Singapore.

Another raging fire has engulfed La Vall d’Uixo, north of Valencia, where a 70-year-old man was found dead inside his car by firefighters.

The vicious inferno has been branded “out of control” by local fire crews as huge swathes of land continue to burn.

Around 45,000 hectares have already been scorched across central provinces around Madrid.



The raging inferno was described as being “at its peak” over the weekend and “beyond the capacity” of firefighters to control.

Madrid emergency management chief Carlos Novillo told the BBC: “It is not possible to attack the fire in that area, so defensive measures are being taken.”

Madrid president Isabel Díaz Ayuso said the inferno was “the worst fire in the history of the region”.

Díaz Ayuso has called the crisis “catastrophic” as residents in the capital were warned to stay indoors and avoid going out unless absolutely necessary.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Dramatic footage has also shown police kicking down doors to rescue residents moments before flames consumed their homes.



And the searing conditions are showing little sign of easing, with Ibiza facing temperatures of up to 36C across parts of the Mediterranean island in the coming days.

News.title: Socialist Spain only has itself to blame for migrants after putting their rights above locals – UK must stop same error
News.content:
IF you want to see how not to handle an immigration crisis look no further than Spain.

Their Socialist prime minister Pedro Sanchez launched an amnesty for undocumented (ie illegal) migrants in April, seemingly, expecting only half a million to apply.



By 30th June, the deadline for applications, some 1.2million had sought to stay in the EU nation legally.

All they needed to qualify was having lived in Spain for five months and having no criminal convictions.



Then earlier this month the Spanish Supreme Court ruled that the sea is not a border and that the authorities could not quickly deport migrants who swim to Spanish territory. They could await the outcome of their application in mainland Spain.

This week we have seen the consequences in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta in North Africa, with around 50-60,000 migrants – equivalent to towns the size of Luton or Reading – swimming over from neighbouring Morocco and walking unchallenged into Spanish territory. [That is equivalent to the population of Basingstoke or Rochdale.]

The migrant amnesty has led to more people trying to get into Spain with many no doubt chancing their arm across the English Channel.

Senor Sanchez and his ultra-left-wing ministers are putting the rights of asylum seekers above those of their own citizens (sound familiar?)



Sánchez called it an “attack” on Spain, but he has only himself to blame.

We should all learn from his monumental error of judgement, one on a par with Angela Merkel’s in 2015, when she flung open the door to a million migrants with a casual wave of the hand, saying, “We can manage this.”

News.title: Funeral director Robert Bush jailed after leaving bodies - including baby - to decompose
News.content:
Former Legacy funeral director Robert Bush gave bereaved families the wrong ashes and left bodies decomposing in what one relative described as 'the most horrendous horror story'

Vile former undertaker Robert Bush - who gave bereaved families the wrong ashes and left the bodies of 35 people, including a stillborn baby, decomposing - has been sentenced to 20 years in prison.

Bush, 48, from Otley, West Yorkshire, hung his head low and repeatedly blinked as he listened to the sentencing remarks at Hull Crown Court - but there were no tears or visible signs of emotion.

Judge Mr Justice Hilliard told the sentencing hearing that he has never "known offences affect so many people and so many people so deeply". When he told the court that Bush had shown regret and that it seemed genuine, many victims' families shook their heads. One woman broke down in silent tears.

Outside court, Karen Dry, whose parents' funerals were organised by Bush, called for a public inquiry into how his crimes were possible, saying: "We all deserve dignity in death and this was totally denied to our loved ones."

Bush was sentenced for 67 offences spanning 12 years and affecting hundreds of victims at his business, Legacy Independent Funeral Directors, in Hull. His victims included the mum of a stillborn baby boy, who discovered that her child's remains had been left on a floor for two years.

You can follow live footage of the sentencing here.

News.title: Betfred store closures confirmed as 132 sites shut and hundreds of jobs lost
News.content:
Betfred store closures confirmed as 132 sites shut and hundreds of jobs lost

Betfred plans to close 132 locations, impacting more than a tenth of its betting shops - leaving the firm with around 1,100 shops across the UK

View Image Betfred is to close 132 shops (stock image) (Image: Getty Images)

More than 600 jobs are to be lost with Betfred planning to shut 132 shops from September.

‌



The company said it has launched a consultation over the closures, which will hit more than a tenth of its betting shops.

‌



The move will leave Betfred with around 1,100 sites across the UK.

‌



Warrington-based Betfred was founded by brothers Fred and Peter Done in 1967. The pair have an estimated wealth of £3.61 billion, according to the most recent Sunday Times Rich List.

Jo Whittaker, chief executive of Betfred, said that the shops are "well-run" with "dedicated colleagues". But, he claimed the company has been left with no choice other than to close them due to economic pressures and taxation.

UK wildfires map shows areas most at risk from infernos as fire rages near nuclear plant READ MORE :

She said: “We have tried hard to protect all our sites and the colleagues who work in them, but the combined impact of higher employer national insurance contributions, wage inflation, increases in gambling taxes and wider economic uncertainty has left us with no choice.

‌



“These are well-run shops, staffed by dedicated colleagues, and it is incredibly hard to see any of them close, but the current fiscal and regulatory environment has made it impossible to keep trading all our shops.

“Our priority now is to support the colleagues affected, and to continue serving customers and communities across the rest of our estate.”

Rival gambling operators Paddy Power and William Hill have also shut dozens of stores over the past year.

‌



In January, William Hill and 888 owner Evoke said it moved “quickly and decisively” to offset recent budget changes to gambling taxes through shop closures and cost cuts.

Last October, Paddy Power revealed plans to shut 57 betting shops across the UK and Ireland, in a move which put 250 workers at risk.

The closure plans come on the back of tax increases announced by the previous chancellor.

Article continues below

Measures announced in last year’s autumn budget saw an increase in remote gaming duty from 21 per cent to 40 per cent, while there will also be a new online sports betting duty of 25 per cent, which will cover all sports except horse racing, from 2027.

Betfred also highlighted pressure from other tax increases including the rise in National Insurance contributions and changes to thresholds.

News.title: Suffolk wildfire live: Dunwich Heath blaze rages as evacuees told situation 'unstable'
News.content:
A wildfire ravaging Dunwich Heath in Suffolk is still 'unstable' according to the local council with the number of firefighters at the scene increasing

A wildfire that has already destroyed a massive area of land in Suffolk and forced scores of people to evacuate remains "unstable" days after it first ignited, the county council has warned.

The blaze at Dunwich Heath has devastated wildlife habitats which could now reportedly take up to 25 years to recover after it went up in flames at about 5pm on Wednesday before engulfing an area equivalent to about 140 football pitches near Sizewell B nuclear power plant.

People evacuated from a local caravan site have now been given a short window to collect their belongings but Peter Langford, emergency planning officer for Suffolk County Council, warned them: "It is still a fast moving situation. From the fire perspective, is still an unstable situation.

"In fact, they've increased a number of pumps back there and they're just about to bring in the helicopter as well." On Thursday afternoon, an EDF spokesperson said the fire was "not affecting operations at Sizewell B power station".

Another wildfire that ignited near Colchester today has now been extinguished after dozens of firefighters rushed to tackle the flames.

News.title: FIFA chief accuses Gianni Infantino of DECEIVING staff over World Cup plot - 'If I lose my job so be it'
News.content:
FIFA chief accuses Gianni Infantino of DECEIVING staff over World Cup plot - 'If I lose my job so be it'

The FIFA president, Gianni Infantino, has come under significant fire over plans to sell stakes in FIFA tournaments such as the World Cup to private investors

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has been accused of 'deceiving' staff with his World Cup sale plot (Image: GSI/Icon Sport via Getty Images)

The chief operating officer of FIFA has accused Gianni Infantino of 'deceiving' staff in relation to the plot to sell World Cup stakes to private investors, adding the proposal 'must not go ahead'.

‌



Infantino unveiled plans to sell off a portion of FIFA's commercial businesses, including tournaments such as the World Cup and the Club World Cup, to private investors. However, his proposal has been met with a ferocious backlash from football's other governing bodies including UEFA, whose nations are ready to boycott future World Cups if the plans go ahead.

‌



One of the 56-year-old's senior advisors, Carlos Cordeiro, has already resigned over the plans. And now another of Infantino's colleagues has torn into the proposal.

‌



Kevin Lamour, who has been FIFA's COO since 2024, says Infantino “deceived” staff with his scheme in a damning statement shared with AP, saying they “deserve better than contempt and intimidation.”

Gianni Infantino ally quits as FIFA boss blasted over World Cup plans in angry statement READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino gets fresh reality check as World Cup boycott grows amid calls for change READ MORE :

“It is the project of one person,” Lamour said. “Not only must this project not go ahead … but the time has now come for football political leaders to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions.”

Lamour, who also worked with Infantino at UEFA previously, did not resign from his post like Cordeiro but added: “And if that means I lose my job, then so be it. I will understand and respect that decision. At least I’ll sleep well tonight.”

‌



View 2 Images FIFA COO Kevin Lamour has hit out at Infantino and his plans

His comments come hot on the heels of Cordeiro deciding to resign from his post over the plans, which prompted UEFA to confirm their nations will boycott future tournaments if they go ahead.

“I cannot stand by while FIFA considers selling a stake in the World Cup,” Cordeiro said.

Article continues below

“Let me be clear. I had no involvement in this proposal, and I oppose it unequivocally,” he added, describing the proposed $20 billion commercial subsidiary as a “bad deal for football”.

News.title: Manchester election results LIVE: By-election set to go to second count as Labour 'confident'
News.content:
Reform council chief threatens to report café owner who gives free meals to hungry kids to police

A café owner who served up free meals to hungry children after food vouchers were removed has been told he will be reported to police by a Reform council leader.

Barry Ashley, who runs the Grumpy Cook in Hastings, stepped up after East Sussex County Council decided not to issue school holiday meal vouchers to struggling families over the summer. He has criticised the move, which he branded “shameless”, accusing the council of turning its back of children in poverty.

He has since been told by Andy Woolley, who heads the authority, that he will be reported to police along with Labour MP Helena Dollimore. Mr Woolley claims to have been personally attacked online and accused the pair of inciting hate and potential violence by naming him in their criticism.

The dispute follows the council's decision not to continue offering the vouchers, which are a lifeline to families. An appalled Mr Ashley responded by announcing he would offer free meals to children who need feeding at his not-for-profit cafe.

A number of local businesses have donated to help, and Mr Ashley told The Mirror he has been providing more than 70 free meals a day. Ms Dollimore has launched a petition calling for the vouchers to be reinstated, branding the council's actions "totally unacceptable" and accusing it of putting children at risk.

Mr Ashley said: "Hastings is one of the poorest towns in the country. And it is by every measure it's a deprived town. One in three of the children are living in poverty.

"And the vouchers, just to take those away without considering what they should be putting in place, without doing any risk assessment, without doing any impact assessment, it's beyond bizarre."

News.title: Britain's sickest funeral director Richard Bush devastated grieving relatives to fund his fantasy lifestyle
News.content:
Britain's sickest funeral director Richard Bush devastated grieving relatives to fund his fantasy lifestyle

Softly-spoken undertaker Robert Bush, with his mealy-mouthed platitudes, was always ready for grieving relatives - but was addicted to life in the fast lane and the high-speed fantasy lifestyle was funded by the bereaved people he conned

Inside funeral parlour where owner gave ashes to wrong families and left bodies to rot

Robert Bush was a funeral director with two faces.

‌



Front of house he was all charm and compassion, softly telling grieving customers; ‘Oh bless you’ while touching his heart as they told him about their loss.

‌



He’d pat their arms gently as he escorted them out, promising their loved ones were now in safe hands.

‌



But it was all fake - even his voice - and the grim reality lurking behind the funeral parlour doors was carnage, chaos... and 35 rotting bodies.

The softly-spoken undertaker, with his mealy-mouthed platitudes, was always ready for grieving relatives... but was addicted to life in the fast lane. His high-speed fantasy lifestyle was funded by the bereaved people he conned.

View 6 Images Bush has been on bail since the bodies were discovered and here on one of his regular dog walks (Image: NB PRESS LTD)

‌



'Monster' funeral director Robert Bush jailed for 20 years as heartbroken families demand public inquiry READ MORE :

Watch as Judge sentences Hull funeral director and families react as 'heartless' Robert Bush jailed READ MORE :

An expert who studied pictures of Bush’s customised superbikes and top-of-the range leathers for the Mirror, believed his passion for motorbikes could have set him back a six-figure sum. The court had only been told he’d spent a more modest £21,000 on his motor racing hobbies.

Today, Robert Bush was sentenced for 67 offences spanning 12 years, including keeping bodies for months, selling dodgy funeral plans, stealing charity donations and handing back the ashes of strangers, even in one case of an animal, to relatives who believed they were receiving the last remains of their loved ones.

Horrified victims have told how they felt comforted by this ‘endearing’ man and the serenity of his chapel of rest at Legacy Funeral Services premises in Hessle Road, Hull.

‌



His desk was free of clutter, surrounded by thank you cards from unsuspecting families. One of those cards could have been from Jasmine Beverley, a grieving mum, sent when she had no idea her stillborn son, Sunny Beverley-Conlin, was hidden a few feet away in a paper bag.

Jasmine recalled Bush's traditional manners and calming air: “He was like a proper old-fashioned gentleman," she said. "I put £20 in a card to say thank you. When I gave it to him, he touched his heart and thanked me.

View 6 Images Bush's police mugshot after being arrested (Image: Humberside Police)

‌



“His properties all looked olde-worldey and you think ‘this is nice' and 'I would like my loved one to be here’. But it was all a show, behind those doors it was a different story and that’s the part he was hiding from us.”

Jasmine points out that even his voice was fake: “When I saw his arrest video his voice had changed, it was different when he spoke to us. He was so well spoken and calming to us. But after his second arrest the mask slipped and he was a different person.”

To the outside world, teetotal Bush, 48, could not have been more respectable. He is originally from the seaside resort of Bridlington, East Yorkshire and was the son of a headmistress. His wife, Vicky was once believed to have been his mum’s deputy at the school where she taught.

‌



Vicky, 53, was listed as a director of Legacy and enjoyed theatre trips to London and meals in Covent Garden with her husband and holidayed at Center Parcs. She is now believed to be retired.

The court heard she received £52,000 a year on average from the funeral business, but Bush was at pains to tell the police his wife and daughter had no idea about the illegal goings-on there. He told one officer: “My wife never even worked for the business. She was on the payroll for tax purposes.”

The family lived together in a detached £400,000 bungalow in the upmarket Hull suburb of Kirk Ella for more than 10 years. The property is now derelict and, according to locals, has recently been sold with the front garden now overgrown with weeds.

‌



View 6 Images Bush would post pictures of him on his customised bikes capable of speeds of more than 180mph

Respectable Bush, who apparently suggested he'd once worked in the prison service and military in his early years, was well regarded by his neighbours. They would see him walking his two little white Maltipoo dogs every day and continuing the charm offensive, saying ‘bless you’ as they crossed paths.

They recall the dad-of-two and his oldest daughter shared a passion for super-bikes, having at least one each and both posting about it on Instagram. Five times a year he would head off to race track days at Caldwell Park in Lincolnshire, riding there in top of the range leathers - which were stored carefully side by side at Legacy, treated with a lot more respect than bodies nearby.

‌



Disgraced funeral director Robert Bush sentenced to 20 years

Bush had a seven-ton truck with its own mobile garage on the back to transport his cherished motorbikes. Neighbours said he used to complain about the cost of the track fees.

The family also owned a jet ski at one time which he used to take on a trailer to the Seven Lakes Country Park caravan and water sports centre at Crowle in Lincolnshire, staying in a static caravan.

‌



Locals say his eldest daughter went into the family business after finishing university with a degree in engineering, but later started work selling medical supplies. His youngest daughter was just 17 when he was arrested. The court heard his offending had also 'devastated' their lives.

View 6 Images Bush's former family home is now overgrown and believed to be on the market

One neighbour said: “They just kept together as a family. They walked the two poodles and kept their girls close to their hearts. They didn’t have many friends. The girls were into super-bikes themselves. They used to bring trial bikes home and ride up and down the street.

‌



“It was funny. Because the majority of people around here are old people. The girls used to do lovely gifts for all the old people at Christmas and Easter.

“No one ever really visited, apart from both sets of elderly parents. She recently lost her mother. They had a nice do for that while other people were rotting in the shed.”

Another neighbour said: “They came across as really family orientated. Like they were really caring. When we moved in five years ago my husband was extending the house at the back. Mr Bush offered to help but then said he could not dig.

‌



“They altered the layout of the bungalow to accommodate Mrs Bush’s sick mother but she died before she could move in. It was about two years ago, just before the scandal broke. The funeral was a low-key, one-hearse affair.”

Another neighbour said: “They don’t drink any alcohol. When I said, ‘You will have to come and have a glass of wine with us', his wife says ‘We only drink homemade lemonade'.

“Even after his arrest, he still kept coming to the house to take all his stuff out. Even though he was on remand. He was coming and picking up his bikes and all sorts. He used to come with his cap pulled down over his face.” A proceeds of crime hearing is to be held at a later date in Hull.

‌



Another man who lives nearby said of Bush’s expensive hobby: “I have a bike myself. To run a super-bike costs about a quarter of a million quid a year.” They used to even have a specialist van come with diagnostics and auto turning, according to the neighbours.

A motorbike expert in Yorkshire, who did not wish to be named, studied the leathers and bikes he’d stored at Legacy said: “If you are really into your bike it can be a money pit and you can spend tens of thousands on it. It is quite a common occurrence for motorcyclists to spend all their money on it.

View 6 Images Bush would build sheds in the back garden for all his motorbike extras

‌



“From a look at his leathers these are the pinnacle and you can see from the scuff marks they’ve fallen off quite a bit. It wouldn’t surprise me if he spent more than 100,000 on his hobby.”

He pointed out the Suzuki large capacity bike, a GSX-R 1000R capable of speeds of up to 186mph, could be worth £40,000 each new but even more with Bush as they had been customised.

“There’s been some money sank into them to make them that way,” he said, pointing out the extra bodywork. “Then you‘ve got new suspensions that can be £8,000 and wheels are £2,500 each.”

‌



“The four leather suits themselves could have cost around £6,000 in total with up to £2,000 for the helmets and visors. Looks like he had Alpinestar and Dainese suits, they are often referred to as the pinnacle of motorcycle wear, especially when it comes to leathers.

"One was a female suit and one had a custom-made bum patch on it. That’s when it gets even more expensive. I'm an avid motorcyclist but that does not stop me sorting out priorities in life."

Bush was selling lots of stuff on Facebook market place prior to his arrest - a mortuary fridge, hearses, a Land Rover and stock cars, a horse box, motor cycles and trial bikes.

‌



Another of his victims, Jayne Rimmington whose mum was one of the bodies stored at Legacy, summed up the cruelty of the man, who put his own desires ahead of everything.

“He stood there smiling, handing me the box, when she was still laying there, rotting away! It's a purely evil thing to do. I know a body is only a vessel and the spirit is gone, but she is still my mum. They were the hands I held and the face I kissed. He betrayed her and he betrayed our trust.“

View 6 Images Bush stored his leathers and bikes near the bodies at Legacy

‌



Before making the defence submissions for Bush, his counsel, Richard Wright KC, insisted they do not wish to “minimise” what he had done.

He told the court there are demands for answers, and said: "There's no doubt his priority was not his customers or their loved ones. That lack of priority may be the best explanation that there is. In other words that he prioritised himself, his family and his circumstances over those who entrusted their deceased to his care."

"That may sound callous, but that is perhaps the most sensible explanation there is in his case," Mr Wright added. He described the "horror and the grief" the court had heard and added: "Robert Bush has listened to every statement being read, and he has heard witness after witness castigate his character and pour out their understandable pain and outrage, all rightly directed at him... he has heard, therefore, the human cost of what he has done."

Article continues below

Mr Wright said Bush has "lost his good name" and has been "treated - quite understandably - as a pariah, hated and despited", adding: "And all of that is his fault." About Bush's family, the defence lawyer said: "His offending has devastated their lievs as well as those of his victims."

"He said he apologises for the deception, the indignity and the infliction of a lot of trauma," Mr Wright told the court. Red-faced Bush listened with his head bowed as the submissions were made on his behalf and at one point bowed down his face could not be seen.

"He accepts entirely that this case is not simply about money. It is about the families that placed their trust in him in moments of profound grief," Mr Wright said. But Mr Wright urged the court to "retain perspective", pointing out the figure of 25 years by the prosecution is the starting point for rape and manslaughter.

News.title: MasterChef winner, 37, suddenly dies as friend makes heartbreaking discovery
News.content:
MasterChef winner, 37, suddenly dies as friend makes heartbreaking discovery

TV cook Eren Kaşıkçı, 37, was found dead at his home in Turkey by his business partner, who had been asked to check on him by worried family on Wednesday afternoon

View 3 Images Eren Kaşıkçı was found dead at his home on Wednesday (Image: Jam Press)

A MasterChef winner has been found dead after he passed away suddenly aged 37.

‌



Relatives raised the alarm when TV cook Eren Kaşıkçı could not be reached, He was sadly found dead at his home a short time later.

‌



The 37-year-old’s business partner found his body in the bedroom of his home after he was asked to check on him on Wednesday afternoon.

‌



Paramedics were called and confirmed that Eren had tragically died at the scene. His body has now been taken for an autopsy to establish the exact cause of death.

Prosecutors have opened an investigation into the celebrity chef’s sudden death.

View 3 Images Eren shot to fame after winning the 2021 season of MasterChef Türkiye (Image: Jam Press)

‌



His business partner Mikail Malkoçoğlu told local media that initial assessments at the victim’s home in Istanbul pointed to a “strong possibility” of a heart attack.

Eren, who had 740,000 Instagram fans, shot to fame after winning the 2021 season of MasterChef Türkiye and later returned for the show’s All Star series.

Known by his nickname Kızıl Sakal, meaning Red Beard, he opened his own restaurant Kızıl Sakal Sandwich & Burger in Istanbul following his victory and had been preparing to expand with a new branch.

‌



View 3 Images Eren was known by his nickname Kızıl Sakal, meaning Red Beard (Image: Jam Press)

He studied tourism and trained professionally as a chef, working in Istanbul hotels before becoming head chef at a hotel on the Aegean island of Gökçeada.

Eren is survived by his wife and their young daughter Maya.

Article continues below

A funeral ceremony is due to take place at Yenidoğan Cemevi before burial in his family’s home province of Tokat today (31 July), as reported by creatorzine.com.

The investigation continues.

News.title: Crete wildfire emergency as hurricane-force winds fan Rethymno flames
News.content:
Evacuations across Europe from ferocious wildfire fueled by extreme heat

Evacuations are continuing from the Atlantic coast to the eastern Mediterranean due to wildfires fueled by an extremely hot summer.

Firefighters in Greece, France, Spain and Turkey are all battling some of the worst blazes with further hot weather ahead.

Greece - Approximately 18,200 acres of land have been burned by the multiple fires that broke out in southern Rethymno, Crete. Fire crews having been focusing on the Agia Paraskevi front, while a new fire broke out in Asomatos. The fire has spread to the Kourtaliotiko Gorge and burned part of the palm groves in Preveli.

New wildfires have also broken out in Achaia, in the northwestern Peloponnese, and in the Xiromero area of Aetolia-Acarnania, a region in western Greece while people are now being evacuated from the Athens suburb of Haidari.

France - Firefighters in southwestern France were working to control the last hotspots of a massive wildfire on Friday that has burned an area four times the size of Paris and forced thousands out of their homes.

The blazes that burned 42,000 hectares (about 162 square miles) of pine forest and touristic resort areas in Bordeaux’s Gironde region on the Atlantic coast haven’t spread for several days.

French Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot has urged holidaymakers to be "extremely vigilant" over wildfires ahead of "one of the biggest weekends for travelling of the year".

Spain - Currently the worst situation is in Castellón where the Vall d'Uixó fire remains out of control into its seventh day. The blaze has already burned 9,598 hectares and forced the evacuation of 5,200 people, although recent progress has allowed 2,800 residents to return.

In Zamora, the situation with the devastating Fermoselle fire (11,000 hectares) improved significantly overnight with the imminent return of residents from 12 of the 14 evacuated towns and the end of lockdowns.

In León, the Veguellina fire remains severe (with approximately 300 evacuees), while the situation with fires in San Cipriano and Valdelaloba is improving.

Turkey - A major fire is still raging in the Cine area, about 60 miles inland from the tourist resort of Bodrum. "In Cine, our teams' interventions from the air and the ground will continue until the fire is completely brought under control," Forestry Minister Ibrahim Yumakli said on X.

However wildfire in Antalya's Kaş district and Muğla province which forced evacuations and road closures have been stabilised.

News.content:
Tens of thousands of migrants have entered Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta, with many swimming and using inflatables to travel from Morocco.

Others ran through a gate in the border fence.

The territory's leader, Juan JesÃºs Vivas, said the number of arrivals has been overwhelming resources and urged the Spanish government to intervene.
