News.title: UK economy to flatline, warns Bank of England
News.content:
Britain’s economy is set to almost grind to a halt for the rest of the year, the Bank of England has warned.

Growth will drop to just 0.1pc per quarter, the Bank predicted, slowing sharply after a strong start to 2026.

Higher petrol prices and energy bills, a weak jobs market and rising mortgage costs are all draining confidence and spending power from the economy.

Inflation, which slowed to a 15-month low of 2.6pc in June, is also expected to rise again to 3.2pc later this year, the Bank warned.

Andrew Bailey, the Bank’s Governor, said inflation had “fallen faster than we’d expected” but warned that war in the Middle East would lead to a fresh spike.

He added that growth would “weaken slightly further in the near term as the effects of the conflict weigh further on demand”.

The Bank also predicted that unemployment will rise back above 5pc in the coming months, limiting workers’ ability to ask for higher wages to cope with rising living costs.

It presents a challenging backdrop for Andy Burnham and his Chancellor, John Healey, who have pledged to help voters struggling with the cost of living.

The forecasts came as policymakers led by Mr Bailey held interest rates at 3.75pc.

Although three members of the nine-strong Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) voted for higher rates, up from two at the previous meeting, the Governor dismissed suggestions the Bank is moving towards higher interest rates.

The public should “not… [think] the Bank of England is edging towards a hike,” Mr Bailey said.

“Frankly there is nothing I have said, or any of us have said, along those lines. We took a decision today to leave the Bank Rate unchanged and that is the relevant conclusion.”

Clare Lombardelli, a Deputy Governor, said voting to keep rates at 3.75pc “was not a close judgement”, calling the decision “pretty clear” given slowing inflation in the domestic economy.

Officials are monitoring the economy for any signs that increases in oil, gas and petrol prices caused by the war in Iran are creeping into higher costs and wages in the wider economy.

Mr Bailey said: “The possibility of repeated resumptions of conflict, combined with lower than usual European gas stock levels and a fall in global refining output, mean that risks to energy prices lie to the upside.”

He added: “Reassuringly, there are few signs so far that second-round effects are generating more broad-based inflationary pressures.”

Companies are struggling to pass higher costs on to their customers because of the economy’s weakness, he added.

Workers are typically securing only modest pay rises as the weak jobs market leaves them in a poor position to push for bigger salaries.

Mr Bailey stressed there are still major risks to the outlook given the war and promised to “monitor the situation carefully” and was “ready to adjust our stance”.

“It is our job to ensure that inflation gets back to the 2pc target and stays there, and that is what we will do,” he said.

Borrowing costs dropped in financial markets after the decision.

The Government’s two-year borrowing cost fell from 4.44pc to 4.34pc, the sharpest fall in a month.

The FTSE 250 index of mid-sized UK companies rose 0.8pc to a record high of 24,184.10.

Traders still believe the Bank will raise interest rates twice within a year.

However, Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said rate rises “remain more a threat than a reality”.

He said there was evidence of disinflation in the economy and interest rates could be “cut to 3pc in 2027”, adding: “That’s very different to market pricing for rates to be close to 4.5pc in 2027.”

News.title: Arsonists torch more Ebola clinics as misinformation spirals in DRC
News.content:
Two more Ebola treatment facilities have reportedly been burned down in recent days as health officials struggle to overcome violent public mistrust of medical teams.

At least a dozen facilities have now been attacked since Congo declared its Ebola outbreak amid fear, misinformation and suspicion of outside authorities.

The outbreak is the fastest growing on record and officials said the virus had now killed more than 1,500 people.

The official death toll from the outbreak centred on the north eastern Ituri province of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has risen by 500 in only a week.

Sources told the Telegraph the large jump in deaths was largely caused by a “data harmonisation exercise” between different regions, and the new deaths may not have all happened in the past week.

However, the daily confirmed toll has also continued to climb sharply with the latest government update reporting 50 people dying in the previous 24 hours.

Airfinity, a health analytics firm, said the outbreak “continues to outpace detection and the response” and there is a high chance of it spreading further inside DRC.

News.title: Race for vaccine against new Ebola strain gets $8.5m boost
News.content:
The “most promising” vaccine to tackle the Ebola strain behind an explosive outbreak in the Congo has been given an $8.5 million boost, as researchers race to develop an effective shot.

So far at least 3,360 people have been infected and 1,487 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), in an epidemic triggered by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola.

But unlike past outbreaks of the more common Zaire strain, there are currently no approved vaccines to tackle Bundibugyo.

On Thursday, the Coalition of Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (Cepi) revealed up to $8.5 million of funding for the only single-dose inoculation, which was described as the “most promising vaccine candidate” by the World Health Organization (WHO) in an analysis in May.

It is being developed by researchers at Hilleman Laboratories – a unique partnership between the pharmaceutical giant Merck and the British philanthropic powerhouse Wellcome, which is headquartered in Singapore.

The vaccine candidate is a Bundibugyo version of the Ervebo shot, which was created by Merck (MSD in Europe) and has already been approved for Ebola Zaire.

It uses a rVSV platform, where a modified version of VSV virus is used to train the immune system to react to target pathogens – in this instance, the Bundibugyo species replaces Zaire.

News.title: AMR chatbot could prevent drug-resistant infections in African hospitals
News.content:
A phone-based chatbot advising medics how to prescribe antibiotics has helped raise the quality of care in African hospitals and should stop bugs developing dangerous resistance, developers say.

Staff at four hospitals across Zambia and Kenya have been using two digital tools in a pilot project to try to address one of the world’s biggest health threats.

Anti-microbial resistance (AMR) is caused by germs evolving so that medicines such as antibiotics designed to kill them no longer work.

The menace is linked to nearly five million deaths each year and makes it increasingly difficult to treat infections. The annual death toll could nearly double in the next 25 years, according to some forecasts.

The rise in AMR is being significantly driven by the misuse and overuse of antimicrobials in human medicine and in agriculture.

Using antibiotics when they are not necessary, using the wrong ones, or getting the dosage wrong, all add to the chances that bugs will develop resistance.

With a shortage of new drugs in the development pipeline, one push to defeat AMR has been to get medics to stick to existing prescription, dosage and treatment advice.

The Antibiotic Stewardship Programme through Innovation, Research, and Education (ASPIRE) is trying to give them guidance using technology they already have in their pockets.

News.title: Tottenham new boys score in shoot-out win over Sydney FC
News.content:
Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

The former Liverpool left-back delivered three dangerous crosses which went unconverted, something of a theme for a Spurs team who failed to make the most of long spells of dominance.

James Maddison and Mateus Fernandes were not in the match-day squad, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven and Jean Paul van Hecke have yet to join the group after the World Cup.

There was another impressive showing from 17-year-old prospect Luca Williams-Barnett, who is pushing for first-team opportunities this upcoming season.

Penalties followed the final whistle, with Spurs scoring all four of their spot kicks. Goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, signed on a free transfer this summer, saved one and Sydney FC’s Josh Lacey hit the post to give Spurs the spoils 4-2.

News.title: Recovery aids and building muscle: Welsh weightlifter Laura Hughes answers your questions
News.content:
Laura Hughes first discovered weightlifting while training at her local Crossfit gym, making the transition from amateur gym-goer to competitive lifting.

Now a member of the Welsh national weightlifting squad, the 33-year-old holds the Welsh record for both the snatch and the clean and jerk (the two official competitive lifts in weightlifting) and is currently third overall in the women’s Welsh rankings. Hughes won bronze at this year’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, following on from her third place at the 2018 Games in Australia.

We caught up with her for our Readers Ask series, where industry specialists answer questions from our Telegraph Recommended Reader Panel.

Who inspired you to get into weightlifting?

Olamilekan, South East

Originally, it was lots of different people, particularly general gym goers who were doing weightlifting at my gym. As I’ve grown as an athlete and become more competitive, I’ve had other inspirations.

Most notably, coming into [the Commonwealth Games], it has to be Gareth [Evans], our coach. Looking back at his performance in 2018 when he won his gold medal is so inspiring. [English lifter] Emily Godley was another competitor in 2018. She won the gold medal in my category and I just remember thinking that she was on fire that day.

What are the best exercises for you to build muscle mass?

Norman, Wales

We spend a lot of time doing our main lifts, so snatches, clean and jerks, but we also do lots of pulls and squats. I spend a lot of time doing accessory work to make sure that my body stays healthy, especially being an older athlete. I’ve put on quite a lot of muscle in this last block just from going heavier and pushing my limits with my main lifts.

What advice would you give to people who want to improve their strength?

David, North West

The most important thing is consistency. As long as you’re doing something, do it regularly, even if it’s twice a week. Don’t be afraid of picking up some dumbbells. If you’ve got somebody that can teach you how to lift weights properly, that’s going to be the best option. Do it safely, do it consistently, and don’t be afraid to try new strength exercises.

Sports.title: When can Mykhalio Mudryk play for Chelsea again, and when was his last appearance for the Blues?
Sports.content:
HALIO AGAIN When can Mykhalio Mudryk play for Chelsea again, and when was his last appearance for the Blues?

CHELSEA winger Mykhalio Mudryk has seen his four-year ban from football end early, ahead of the new season.

The Blues signed Mudryk from under the noses of Arsenal in January 2023, but his first spell with the club failed to live up to expectations.



The 25-year-old had scored 10 times in 73 appearances for the Blues, prior to being banned in 2024.

The £80million winger shared a number of training clips on his social media platforms throughout the ban, but new manager Xabi Alonso will be boosted by the ending of the ban.



The Blues are currently on a pre-season tour in Hong Kong, where they will meet Spurs tomorrow.

SunSport can reveal when Mykhalio Mudryk can return for Chelsea, and when his last appearance was.

When can Mykhalio Mudryk play for Chelsea, and when was his last appearance?

After being banned in 2024, he is now available to play immediately for the Blues, but will not join up with Xabi Alonso’s squad until next week.

Mykhalio Mudryk has not played for Chelsea since a 2-0 win in the Conference League against Heidenheim.

The Ukrainian winger was an unused substitute three days later in a 3-0 win over Aston Villa, the last time he was allowed to play.

The 25-year-old is set to join up with Alonso’s squad in Hong Kong, as they prepare for the new Premier League season.



Why was Mykhalio Mudryk banned from playing football?

Mykhalio Mudryk was panned for four years for a positive test of meldonium, a banned cardiovascular substance.

He tested positive for the substance while with Ukraine in late 2024.

Mudryk was suspended in December 2024, and formally charged in January 2025.

In January 2026, he was handed a four-year ban, but has been allowed to return to just six months later.

Sports.title: Newcastle CONFIRM Eddie Howe resignation with five coaches including Jason Tindall shown exit door
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE have confirmed Eddie Howe’s resignation as boss.

And five members of his coaching staff, including assistant Jason Tindall, are following him out the door at St James’ Park.



Howe’s impending exit emerged hours after his side were beaten 4-1 by Bristol City in a pre-season friendly.

In addition to Howe and Tindall, first team coaches Graeme Jones, Stephen Purches and Simon Weatherstone are all leaving the club, as well as head of performance Dan Hodges.



The former Toon boss is set to be replaced by Al-Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle.

Upon confirmation of his decision to leave, Howe released a lengthy statement via Newcastle’s website.

An extract of it read: “After nearly five years of giving my life, heart and soul into the club with unrelenting energy, I feel that it is in the best interests of both myself and the club to step away, recharge and take a break.

“Although it’s been incredibly difficult to make this decision, I know in my heart that it’s the right one. I have always put the best interests of Newcastle before my own in every single decision I have made whilst I’ve been here and this one is no different.

“It has been the privilege of my lifetime to have been the manager of Newcastle United.”

Howe was appointed Newcastle boss in November 2021 shortly after the club’s Saudi takeover.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The former Bournemouth boss twice guided the Toon into the Champions League, while in 2025 he ended their 70-year wait for a domestic trophy by winning the Carabao Cup at Wembley.

Tindall, meanwhile, had succeeded Howe as Cherries manager in August 2020.

But having been sacked after just 31 games at the helm, the long-time No2 joined Howe’s Newcastle staff upon his mate’s arrival at St James’ Park.

Howe took charge of 231 competitive games as Toon boss; winning 112, drawing 48 and losing 71.



Tindall, 48, stood in for Howe for a match against Manchester United in April 2025, when the Newcastle manager was suffering with illness – the Magpies winning the match 4-1.

Sports.title: Newcastle close in on £26million transfer in first move since Eddie Howe’s shock exit
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE are close to securing their first signing of the post-Eddie Howe era.

Amid a turbulent summer on Tyneside, the Magpies are negotiating a fee with Braga goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek according to reports.



Czech shot stopper Hornicek has a £25.7m release clause at the Portuguese outfit, which Newcastle are expected to trigger.

Braga’s first choice keeper was conspicuously absent from their squad for last night’s Europa League qualifier against Železničar Pančevo.



The Toon Army have already had a busy summer between the sticks, turning down the option to buy Aaron Ramsdale after a season-long loan, before signing 20-year-old Ewen Jaouen for £18.5m from Rennes.

Pinning down a successor to Nick Pope was a summer priority for Newcastle, who had previously failed to entice top target James Trafford to the club for the second summer running.

Hornicek, 24, cuts a towering figure at 6ft 6ins, and arrives at St James’ Park on the back of a monumental summer.

The Czech make his international bow this May, just days after starting in a narrow Europa League semi-finals defeat.

He was an unused substitute at the World Cup.

While a multi-million pound move to the Premier League presents a major opportunity, Hornicek arrives at a club in a state of flux.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Eddie Howe‘s sudden and spectacular departure has sent shockwaves around St James’ Park.

The League Cup-winning coach is set to be replaced by Al-Ahli’s Matthias Jaissle in a £9.4 million move.

Alongside personnel changes at the top, Newcastle have been caught up in a transfer whirlpool this summer.

Superstars Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali have left Tyneside for a combined £170 million, while Bruno Guimaraes appears on the brink of a megabucks move to Arsenal.

Sports.title: Mykhailo Mudryk, 25, free to play for Chelsea again after almost two years as drugs ban decision is made
Sports.content:
MYKHAILO MUDRYK has been cleared to return to football after nearly two years of doping hell.

The £80million Chelsea winger has been suspended since December 2024 after meldonium, a prohibited substance, was discovered in a sample provided while on international duty with Ukraine.



Mudryk, 25, was handed a four-year ban, which he has successfully appealed. The Ukraine international is now free to play for the Blues once more.

The winger is due to join Xabi Alonso‘s squad on tour in Hong Kong next week.



He described the ordeal as the most difficult period of his career.

Mudryk said: “After a long battle, the four-year ban that was imposed on me has been rescinded and I am free to resume my career with immediate effect.



“I am grateful that this process has reached a conclusion, that I have been cleared to return to football and that I can now look ahead to my future.

“This has been the most difficult period of my career.

“As I have always maintained from the outset of this case, I have never knowingly or intentionally taken any banned substance.

“My commitment to competing fairly and representing my club and country with professionalism and integrity has always been important to me.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“I would like to thank my family and friends for their support and belief throughout this period.

“I also want to express my deep gratitude to everyone at Chelsea FC, my teammates and the Chelsea supporters who have been with me throughout.

“I would also like to thank my legal team and others who assisted for their tireless work on my case.

“My focus now is on returning to football, working hard every day, and making a positive contribution on the pitch.”



Meldonium was added to the World Anti-Doping Agency’s (WADA) prohibited list in 2016 as it increases endurance, reduces fatigue and shortens recovery times.

During his ban, Mudryk has been training alone to maintain fitness, using pitches at Uxbridge FC and was spotted attending Wimbledon this year.

Changes to doping testing processes mean that were Mudryk’s sample to be tested today, it would not have been reported as a breach.

WADA labs use a testing method by which concentration levels are estimated rather than measured, which has resulted in the reporting threshold being raised.

Mudryk always maintained he did never knowingly or intentionally use meldonium, but accepted he had breached anti-doping rules.



The amount of meldonium in the sample was low, meaning it could have come from an accidental contamination. The exact source of contamination has never been identified.

In a statement, the FA said: “The FA can confirm that the anti-doping disciplinary proceedings against Mykhailo Mudryk were resolved with the agreement of the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) on 30 July 2026.

“In the context of that agreement, Mr Mudryk has accepted his commission of Anti-Doping Rule Violations (ADRVs) and accepted a period of ineligibility.

“On 7 to 9 January 2026, a hearing took place before an independent Regulatory Commission.

“The Regulatory Commission found that Mr Mudryk had committed the charged ADRVs and imposed a four-year period of ineligibility.



“Subsequently, Mr Mudryk filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

“Since then, changes have been made to WADA Technical Document (TD2027MRL) which, while not retroactive, mean that if Mr Mudryk’s sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no ADRVs would have resulted.

“Further to that development and to other circumstances of the case, The FA and Mr Mudryk have now – with the agreement of WADA – resolved the appeal proceedings in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the World Anti-Doping Code and Regulation 90 of the 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations.

“As a part of the agreement, Mr Mudryk accepted that he had committed the Anti-Doping Rule Violations charged and acceded to a period of ineligibility equal to the time served at the date of the agreement.

“Mr Mudryk is no longer ineligible and may return to competition with immediate effect.”



A Chelsea statement read: “From the outset, this has been an extremely difficult period for Misha, both professionally and personally, and we are pleased that the matter has now reached a conclusion which allows him to return to football with immediate effect.

“We have always supported Misha throughout this process while fully respecting the integrity of the anti-doping system and the legal process.

‘Always supported Mudryk’

“Throughout this process he has conducted himself professionally and with resilience during what has undoubtedly been one of the most challenging periods of his career.

“We know how much this opportunity to return means to him. Our focus now is on supporting Misha’s reintegration into the squad and helping him resume his career.

“Chelsea FC remains fully committed to the highest standards of sporting integrity and compliance with all anti-doping regulations.



“Everyone at the club now looks forward to helping Misha return to full fitness, back into the squad and back onto the pitch.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Signed from Shakhtar Donetsk in January 2023, the winger has ten goals in 73 Chelsea appearances and is under contract until 2031.

His last appearance for the club came against Arsenal in November 2024.

Sports.title: Non-league club’s plans for new 8,000-capacity stadium REJECTED over lead pollution concerns
Sports.content:
THE GOVERNMENT has dished out a crushing blow to a non-league club by rejecting their plans for an 8,000-seat stadium.

The proposed £40million development would also have included 3,500 new homes, a hotel, retail and leisure space, and improved roads.



National League South side Ebbsfleet United had the plans approved by Gravesham Borough Council more than TWO YEARS ago.

The centrepiece would have been a glitzy new ground to replace their 4,700-capacity Stonebridge Road venue, which was built in 1905.



But a number of concerns were raised upon closer inspection, including the threat of lead poisoning for future residents due to a nearby refinery, and the loss of jobs by demolishing the Robins Wharf industrial estate.

Britannia Refined Metals insist the 50-acre brownfield site is “not an appropriate location” for the mega build.



The Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government said the refusal of the development was in line with the planning inspector’s recommendations.

But the chairman of Kent-based sixth-tier side Ebbsfleet, Damian Irvine, has lashed out against the decision.

He said: “Northfleet and Gravesham require inward investment.

“For a government that claims to have been builders not blockers and to be reducing red tape and do everything they can, this decision seems to fly in the face of their public words. That’s our gut feeling.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Irvine added on the lead poisoning report: “We have been living and working here for the past decades. That one was confusing to us.

“Should we all be moving out? There are already thousands of people living and working here.”

The club added in a Facebook post: “We are surprised and disappointed at that decision and the timing of it.

“This is particularly so given it is more than two years since Gravesham Borough Council approved the Northfleet Harbourside development and that the housing minister and Secretary of State have been very vocal publicly around their policy of promoting building and development – and reducing red tape – by fast-tracking planning decisions.”

Sports.title: Four reasons it all came crumbling down for Newcastle as bold plan to be best team in the world by 2030 lies in tatters
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE’S ambitious owners made a point of marking 2030 as the year they would become one of the best teams in the world.

It was CEO David Hopkinson’s aim to be “in the debate about being the top club in the world” by 2030.



Now, with less than four years to go until that point, even Eddie Howe has lost faith in the aspirational target.

Howe’s Toon exit is the biggest warning sign yet that the Saudi chiefs in charge on Tyneside have made promises they can’t keep.



Newcastle remain the richest club in world football, yet their approach to rubbing shoulders with the biggest clubs has been wide of the mark.

It took Manchester City just over three and a half years to win their first Premier League title following their 2008 Abu Dhabi takeover.



Newcastle are almost five years into their project and they are heading into the new campaign having lost the best manager in their modern history, with no European football and in the midst of a hellish transfer window.

FINANCIAL TROUBLES

Despite being backed by the wealthiest owners in world football, it appears Newcastle can’t spend any money.

Stringent Financial Fair Play (FFP), Squad Cost Ratio (SCR) and Profit and Sustainability Rules (PSR) have put the Magpies between a rock and a hard place.

They have already breached Uefa’s financial sustainability regulations, and are now in a three-year settlement agreement with the European governing body.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Gone are the days when a club could be taken over and throw unlimited cash at world class players like Robinho.

Newcastle are effectively limited to what they can earn through their own sponsorships and commercial revenue, something which is incredibly hard to generate out of thin air – especially with the 2021 rules on associated party transactions.

Despite more than doubling their annual revenue since the takeover, Newcastle still earn basically half of the average ‘Big Six’ income every year.

That is largely why they have been forced to sell some of their biggest stars and highest rated academy prospects over the last couple of summers.



PLAYER SALES

The last few summers have been nothing short of catastrophic for Newcastle.

The club has been forced into selling Alexander Isak, Sandro Tonali, Anthony Gordon and Elliot Anderson.

Captain Bruno Guimaraes also appears close to joining that list of departures, with the Brazilian edging towards a switch to champions Arsenal.

While the club managed to bring in over £300 million from those players, the funds have largely gone into rebalancing the books and spending on weaker replacements.



Anderson, who left Newcastle for just £35m in 2024, is now the third most expensive player in Premier League history following his £116m move to Man City this summer.

His St James’ Park exit was almost entirely down to FFP rules, with Newcastle needing to shift academy talent for ‘pure profit’ to fund spending elsewhere.

The sales of players like Isak, Tonali and Gordon are examples of football’s natural food chain, regardless of how rich your owners are.

PLAYER PURCHASES

Newcastle’s recruitment story is one of what could have been, rather than what has happened.



That same football food chain has been the Toon Army’s downfall over the last few years.

Eddie Howe pushed for the club to sign players like Joao Pedro, Hugo Ekitike, James Trafford and Benjamin Sesko.

But bigger clubs came knocking and each one of those stars opted for the bright lights of a ‘Big Six’ club over the Magpies’ unrealised potential.

The club’s Saudi chiefs have also had to deal with a ‘Newcastle Tax’ slapped on almost every player they signed, increasing transfer fees given their apparent financial might.

Nick Woltemade cost almost £70m, Anthony Elanga was £60m and Yoane Wissa was remarkably purchased for £55m last summer.



When Newcastle have got their recruitment right – Guimaraes, Tonali, Isak and the like – they were treated as a stepping stone and proved unable to hold onto the talent.

STADIUM WOES

To be considered as one of the biggest clubs in the world you have to act like one.

For Newcastle’s bigwigs, this means having a stadium that matches their ambitions.



The club has already explored redeveloping St James Park, as well as the potential of building a new stadium entirely.

Increased capacity would not only help Newcastle fit in with their rivals but also significantly increase revenue through ticket sales.

The club has already made a “strategic purchase” of most of the listed Leazes Terrace building to make a potential renovation easier.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

However, their grand plans are still not finalised and, no matter which route they take, the project is expected to cost well in excess of £1BILLION.

The club are taking their time with the planning process and even if they began work immediately, completion would likely not come before their 2030 goal.

Sports.title: Chelsea signing Henderson and Welbeck because ‘they have a lot of young boys away with the fairies’, says title winner
Sports.content:
A SIX-TIME Premier League champion has blasted Chelsea’s young stars for being “a bit away with the fairies”.

Treble-winning midfielder Nicky Butt hailed Xabi Alonso‘s attempt to rein in an ill-disciplined dressing room by recruiting veteran duo Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson.



Manchester United legend Butt was blunt about the state of the Blues.

He said: “They’ve got a lot of young boys in that training room that are a bit away with the fairies and doing what they want to do if I’m being honest.



“I’ve seen a few players like that in the training room.

“They’ll be there to get them to knuckle down a bit and I’m pretty sure Xabi Alonso will be thinking about wanting a bit of help in the background.”

Chelsea had the youngest average dressing room age in the league last season, and new manager Alonso was quick to make eyebrow-raising moves for two of the Prem’s senior citizens.

Welbeck, 35, has an incoming medical at Stamford Bridge, and Butt is firmly in favour of the Blues buying their first player over 30 since 2022.

Butt, speaking exclusively to Paddy Power, said: “The Danny Welbeck signing in particular is really good.”

“He’s a great squad lad, great to have on the bench, coming on, starting a few games, scoring your goals, and he’s a good professional.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

However, it came as “a bit more of a shock” to see Chelsea pursuing former England skipper Jordan Henderson.

The former Liverpool legend is the last English captain to lift the Premier League, and covered more kilometres per 90 minutes playing for Brentford last season than any Chelsea player.

Butt was full of praise for the 36-year-old: “Henderson is obviously a fantastic professional as well, been around the block, knows what he’s doing.”

The pair of seasoned pros last played together for England U21s back in 2010/11, and have both reportedly agreed two-year deals with the Blues.



Although the two signings still have enduring class to offer on the pitch, Butt believes the veterans’ true value will be their authoritative influence in the dressing room.

During England’s recent run to the World Cup semi finals, Henderson slotted into a player-coach role, and Butt thinks Chelsea have snapped him up for more of the same.

Sports.title: Five candidates to replace Infantino as Fifa president including Arsene Wenger and chief who boycotted World Cup final
Sports.content:
FIFA could need a new president sooner rather than later after pressure increases on Gianni Infantino – but who would replace the current chief?

Infantino, 56, is facing calls to step down after his plans to sell part of the World Cup to private investors emerged.



If he isn’t ousted in the coming weeks or months, the much-maligned Infantino is only safe in his position until next year anyway.

Fifa members could vote for an alternative candidate at the 2027 election – but there’s a catch.



So far there is no contest for Infantino, who ran unopposed in 2019 and 2023.

He took over from the disgraced Sepp Blatter in the wake of 2015’s corruption scandal.



Infantino has already changed rules allowing him to stand for an unprecedented FOURTH term in charge – which would take him up to 2031 before stepping down.

Then he could potentially go into a role heading Fifa’s proposed new sister company in charge of making world football as much dollar as possible through its business connection and high-rolling investors.

There, he stands to earn a potentially staggering £1MILLION each week.

But none of this is guaranteed. Fifa could back down from their greedy shakeup after all 55 Uefa nations agreed to boycott upcoming events – including future women’s and youth World Cup.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Currently, Infantino is holding his ground. But senior advisor Carlos Cordeiro has RESIGNED over the controversy.

And Uefa are now thought to be preparing someone to stand against Infantino next year in the Fifa elections.

But who could take on the sport’s most powerful man? And if the net is cast wider than just Europe, are there any better solutions?

Alexander Ceferin

Perhaps the obvious name, Uefa president Ceferin is extremely well placed.



He has been in a battle with Fifa for years and has spoken out against them around high-profile situations including Folarin Balogun‘s overturned red card.

Ceferin didn’t even bother going to the World Cup final despite Spain being in it.

He is said to be happy in his position – which has been held since 2016 – which is expected to go on for a third term until 2031.

The Slovenian is described as happy to step up if nobody else will, but is not keen to move unless absolutely necessary.

Nasser Al-Khelaifi

That brings up PSG president Al-Khelaifi, who is one of the early favourites to challenge – and possibly succeed – Infantino.



He is also in charge of the European Football Clubs (EFC) and opposed the European Super League in 2021.

However, a representative of the Qatari is quoted as saying: “Nasser has absolutely no ambition, no intention, no interest in the Fifa role, and he will continue to discreetly support all the institutions of world and European football.”

Some reports suggest he could yet make a play.



Arsene Wenger

Former Arsenal boss Wenger has been on Fifa’s side for years, floating outrageous rule changes every now and then.

He is officially the Chief of Global Football Development and stays relatively quiet,

But with Wenger’s heft in the game and some backing, could he rise up against Infantino from within?



Victor Montagliani

Outside of Fifa and Uefa, Concacaf president Montagliani was a touted candidate for the presidency before all of this kicked off.

The Canadian has been claimed to have harboured interests in becoming top dog for a while as Infantino’s public popularity continued to wain in the build-up to – and during – the World Cup.

His term in North America and the Caribbean comes to an end next year and he is seeking another term.

But maybe he will go one up and rebel against Infantino instead.

Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa

Like Uefa and Concacaf – to a lesser extent – the AFC has spoken out against selling the World Cup.



And president Al Khalifa, from Bahrain, is an important figure with his fingers in at Fifa as well.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He is the senior vice-president of the Fifa Council and has joined the Infantino pile on.

Like Montagliani, he has a confederation election next year to think about as well as the possible Fifa one.

Sports.content:
Real Madrid make final Vinicius Jr decision as Arsenal put on transfer red alert

Vinicius Jr has just one year left on his deal at Real Madrid and Arsenal hope to tempt the forward to join them at the Emirates Stadium this summer

View 2 Images Vinicius Junior is a transfer target for Arsenal (Image: (Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty Images))

Real Madrid have tabled a final take it or leave it contract offer to Vinicius Junior as he continues to attract interest from Arsenal. The Gunners have enquired about the Brazil international, as boss Mikel Arteta wants to sign proven talent this summer.

‌



Vinicius fits the bill, winning 14 trophies and scoring 128 goals in 375 matches for the Spanish giants, but he only has one year remaining on his current deal. Real have tried to renew Vinicius' deal and opened further talks with him earlier this week, but with no progress made, they have now hit their star man with an ultimatum.

‌



According to Spanish publication Marca, the La Liga giants have informed the 26-year-old’s camp that the latest contract offer they submitted is final and there will be no further increase nor another round of negotiations. If Vinicius accepts, his deal will be renewed, however, if he rejects the offer Real will open the door to a sale this summer to prevent the Brazilian from entering his final year of contract year and leaving for free later, according to Marca.

‌



The Gunners have already bolstered their attacking options this summer with the £34million signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge earlier this month. Arteta admitted he will 'require a better squad and better individuals' for the forthcoming season in an interview with the club’s inhouse media channels earlier this week.

He said: “This has to be the start and this has to be the standard. Excellence has to be our standard and this has to drive us to attack the future.

Sports.title: Matthias Jaissle can hand Newcastle chance to sign title winner and help fill Anthony Gordon void
Sports.content:
Matthias Jaissle can hand Newcastle chance to sign title winner and help fill Anthony Gordon void

Newcastle United look to be closing in on appointing Matthias Jaissle as the replacement for Eddie Howe.

View 2 Images Newcastle United look set to appoint Matthias Jaissle as their new head coach. (Image: Yasser Bakhsh/Getty Images))

It’s set to be all change for Newcastle United this summer, both in the dugout and on the pitch. After five years in charge of the club, Eddie Howe has left St James’ Park.

‌



The news broke just a matter of hours after the 4-1 friendly defeat against Championship side Bristol City. It seems to be a time of Chaos for Newcastle.

‌



The manager is said to have made the decision, which follows the sales of Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon earlier this summer. Gordon moved to Barcelona for a fee of £69.3 million, with Tonali completing a £100 million transfer to Tottenham.

‌



The Premier League special edition is on sale now READ MORE :

Bruno Guimaraes pushes for Arsenal transfer with Newcastle agreement imminent READ MORE :

There is also speculation over the futures of both Bruno Guimaraes and Lewis Hall. Arsenal are being strongly linked with Guimaraes , and Manchester United interested in Hall.

For Newcastle, the focus will be on bringing in replacements for Howe and handling any outgoings between now and the Premier League opener. The Magpies seem to be closing in on a deal for Al-Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle.

If that appointment is made, then it could potentially open up the door for Newcastle to move for a former Premier League title winner, who could help to fill some of the void of the quality left by the sales.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

While at Al-Ahil, Jaissle has worked closely with Riyad Mahrez. Under the German coach, he played 122 games, scoring 37 times and providing 50 assists.

The 35-year-old officially left the club this summer and is now available on a free transfer. He could be a player who Jaissle could turn to as he looks to make an impact at Newcastle.

‌



Mahrez’s age and the fact that he has been playing in Saudi Arabia means that he may not be expected to start every game. Newcastle have already brought in a replacement for Gordon in Bazoumana Toure.

View 2 Images Riyad Mahrez is available on a free transfer this summer. (Image: Ercin Erturk/Anadolu via Getty Images)

But, Mahrez, who has won five Premier League titles with Leicester City and Manchester City, would no doubt add some Premier League know-how and quality to Newcastle’s squad.

‌



Speaking about his relationship with Mahrez in December 2024, Jaissle told RMC Sport: "Mahrez is a fantastic footballer, I have a very good relationship with him. And I think if you ask him, he'll probably tell you the same thing.

“I can only say that I'm really happy to have him on the team. He's an incredible player, he's won everything. And he's showing it again this year with the difference he's able to make during matches.”

Mahrez captained Algeria in this summer’s World Cup, scoring twice and providing an assist in his four appearances in the competition. He announced his retirement from international football following the tournament, meaning he’ll be concentrating on his club career.

Article continues below

Fabrizio Romano reports that he is keen to return to Europe, with Serie A Clubs showing an interest. Despite his age, having the chance to sign someone of Mahrez’s quality may be one that Newcastle shouldn’t turn down.

Sports.content:
Chelsea and FA drop Mykhailo Mudryk statement

Mykhailo Mudryk will now be available to play for Chelsea. A statement from the FA confirmed the news, saying: "The FA can confirm that the anti-doping disciplinary proceedings against Mykhailo Mudryk were resolved with the agreement of the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) on 30 July 2026.

"In the context of that agreement, Mr Mudryk has accepted his commission of Anti-Doping Rule Violations (ADRVs) and accepted a period of ineligibility. On 22 October 2024, Mr Mudryk was subject to an out-of-competition doping control, which revealed the presence of a low concentration of meldonium, a prohibited substance.

"The FA notified Mr Mudryk of that finding on 4 December 2024 and imposed a provisional suspension. On 23 May 2025, The FA charged Mr Mudryk with ADRVs in breach of Regulations 3 and 4 of its 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations.

"On 7 to 9 January 2026, a hearing took place before an independent Regulatory Commission. The Regulatory Commission found that Mr Mudryk had committed the charged ADRVs and imposed a four-year period of ineligibility. Subsequently, Mr Mudryk filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

"Since then, changes have been made to WADA Technical Document (TD2027MRL) which, while not retroactive, mean that if Mr Mudryk's sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no ADRVs would have resulted.

"Further to that development and to other circumstances of the case, The FA and Mr Mudryk have now - with the agreement of WADA - resolved the appeal proceedings in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the World Anti-Doping Code and Regulation 90 of the 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations.

"As a part of the agreement, Mr Mudryk accepted that he had committed the Anti-Doping Rule Violations charged and acceded to a period of ineligibility equal to the time served at the date of the agreement. Mr Mudryk is no longer ineligible and may return to competition with immediate effect."

Chelsea also uploaded their own statement which said: "Chelsea FC acknowledges today's announcement by The Football Association confirming the resolution of the anti-doping proceedings involving Mykhailo Mudryk.

"From the outset, this has been an extremely difficult period for Misha, both professionally and personally, and we are pleased that the matter has now reached a conclusion which allows him to return to football with immediate effect.

"We have always supported Misha throughout this process while fully respecting the integrity of the anti-doping system and the legal process. We welcome the acknowledgement that advances in the applicable scientific reporting standards for more reliable testing mean that, had Misha's sample been analysed under today's technical requirements, it would not have been reported as a positive test and no anti-doping rule violation would have resulted.

"That is an important part of the context surrounding the agreed resolution and allows everyone involved to move forward. "Misha has consistently maintained that he never knowingly or intentionally used a prohibited substance and did not know how traces of the substance entered his system. Throughout this process he has conducted himself professionally and with resilience during what has undoubtedly been one of the most challenging periods of his career.

"We know how much this opportunity to return means to him. Our focus now is on supporting Misha’s reintegration into the squad and helping him resume his career. Chelsea FC remains fully committed to the highest standards of sporting integrity and compliance with all anti-doping regulations. Everyone at the Club now looks forward to helping Misha return to full fitness, back into the squad and back onto the pitch."

Sports.title: Newcastle United confirm Eddie Howe exit with statement issued as replacement lined up
Sports.content:
Newcastle United confirm Eddie Howe exit with statement issued as replacement lined up

Eddie Howe ended Newcastle United's barren run without a major trophy but will now depart the club after nearly five years of service

View 2 Images Eddie Howe has walked away from his role as Newcastle United boss (Image: MI News/NurPhoto)

Newcastle United have confirmed Eddie Howe has resigned from his position as manager. Earlier reports had stated the Englishman was set to walk away from the club after nearly five years at the helm.

‌



He was the first permanent manager to be appointed by the club after the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund's takeover toward the end of 2021. The ex-Bournemouth manager guided the Magpies into the Champions League on two occasions and won the League Cup to end their 70-year wait without a trophy.

‌



However, things grew more difficult for Howe when Alexander Isak joined Liverpool for £125million and while around £240m was spent on new signings, the club struggled to a 12th placed Premier League finish. After seeing Anthony Gordon join Barcelona, Sandro Tonali join Tottenham Hotspur for £100m and Bruno Guimaraes inform the club he also wants to depart, Howe's resignation has been confirmed.

‌



Newcastle confirmed the news in a statement, which read: "Newcastle United can announce that Eddie Howe has informed the club of his decision to step down as head coach.

Bruno Guimaraes pushes for Arsenal transfer with Newcastle agreement imminent READ MORE :

Bruno Guimaraes given separate Newcastle plan as showdown transfer talks scheduled READ MORE :

"The club has accepted Eddie’s decision and would like to thank him for his extraordinary contribution.

"Also leaving the club are coaches Jason Tindall, Graeme Jones, Stephen Purches and Simon Weatherstone, and head of performance Dan Hodges."

‌



Howe went on to issue an emotional farewell message to Newcastle fans, with the 48-year-old saying: “After a period of personal reflection, I have decided that now is the right time for me to step away from my role as head coach of Newcastle United.

“After nearly five years of giving my life, heart and soul into the club with unrelenting energy, I feel that it is in the best interests of both myself and the club to step away, recharge and take a break.

“Although it’s been incredibly difficult to make this decision, I know in my heart that it’s the right one. I have always put the best interests of Newcastle before my own in every single decision I have made whilst I’ve been here and this one is no different.

‌



“It has been the privilege of my lifetime to have been the manager of Newcastle United.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

“It is difficult to put into words what this club, the city and its supporters mean, and will always mean, to me and my family. From the moment myself, Jason and all of the staff arrived nearly half a decade ago, Newcastle instantly felt like home and the people here welcomed us with open arms. We took huge pride in representing the club from day one and this city will always hold a very special place in our hearts.

‌



“There have been so many incredible moments in our time here. From fighting relegation in our first season to the numerous unforgettable nights at St. James’ Park in the Champions League soon after. The progression was fast.

“Everyone came together, united and what a force we became, culminating in bringing home our first domestic trophy in 70 years. These are all memories that I will cherish for the rest of my life.

“I would like to put on record my sincere thanks and appreciation to Yasir Al-Rumayyan, Jamie Reuben, Jacobo Solís and everyone at PIF, David Hopkinson, Ross Wilson and the entire ownership and leadership group for placing their trust in me and for giving me the opportunity to lead this special football club.

‌



“I remain incredibly positive and enthusiastic about the future of Newcastle. The club is in fantastic hands with a great leadership team and I have no doubt together, alongside whoever comes in to replace me, they will continue to deliver success on the pitch.

View 2 Images Eddie Howe has officially left Newcastle United (Image: David Davies/PA Wire)

“Thank you to Jason Tindall, Graeme Jones, Stephen Purches, Simon Weatherstone, Dan Hodges, Andy Howe and Jordan Tribe for their incredible loyalty, support and dedication and to all of the amazing staff behind the scenes whose hard work and loyalty makes this club what it is.

‌



“A special thank you to all of the players who have represented the club during my time here. Without you, nothing would have been possible and it’s been an honour to have coached you all.

“Finally, and most importantly, thank you to our incredible supporters. Your passion and loyalty have inspired me every single day. To stand on the touchline at St. James’ Park as your manager with the honour of representing your club has meant more to me than you will ever know.

“While my journey as manager has now come to an end, the affinity and love I will always hold for Newcastle United never will.

‌



“Thank you for everything. I wish the club every success for the future.”

Matthias Jaissle, 38, is expected to become the next Newcastle manager having previously coached Saudi Arabian side Al-Ahli, who he guided to two Asian Cup titles, the continent's version of the Champions League.

Chelsea star Mykhailo Mudryk shares emotional message after doping ban lifted

Mykhailo Mudryk has had his suspension from football lifted and been given the green light to return to playing, with the Chelsea winger poised to join the club's pre-season tour in Hong Kong.

Sports.title: Mykhailo Mudryk ban LIFTED as FA release statement confirming Chelsea star can play again
Sports.content:
Mykhailo Mudryk ban LIFTED as FA release statement confirming Chelsea star can play again

Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk has been on the sidelines since December 2024 after testing positive for a banned substance but the Ukrainian is now available to play for the Blues once again

View 2 Images Mykhaylo Mudryk has been banned sinced December 2024 (Image: Getty Images)

Chelsea star MykhaIlo Mudryk is now free to play for the club again, the FA have announced.

‌



The Ukrainian wideman was provisionally banned in December 2024 after testing positive for a banned substance. He has not played for the club since.

‌



But the FA have now confirmed that his ban has been lifted due to changes in the WADA guidlines. A statement from the FA read: "The FA can confirm that the anti-doping disciplinary proceedings against Mykhailo Mudryk were resolved with the agreement of the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) on 30 July 2026. In the context of that agreement, Mr Mudryk has accepted his commission of Anti-Doping Rule Violations (ADRVs) and accepted a period of ineligibility.

‌



"On 22 October 2024, Mr Mudryk was subject to an out-of-competition doping control, which revealed the presence of a low concentration of meldonium, a prohibited substance. The FA notified Mr Mudryk of that finding on 4 December 2024 and imposed a provisional suspension. On 23 May 2025, The FA charged Mr Mudryk with ADRVs in breach of Regulations 3 and 4 of its 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations. "On 7 to 9 January 2026, a hearing took place before an independent Regulatory Commission. The Regulatory Commission found that Mr Mudryk had committed the charged ADRVs and imposed a four-year period of ineligibility. Subsequently, Mr Mudryk filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

Danny Welbeck's Chelsea comments backfire with awkward Brighton reunion weeks away READ MORE :

How Chelsea managed to escape Premier League points deduction as FA explain charges READ MORE :

"Since then, changes have been made to WADA Technical Document (TD2027MRL) which, while not retroactive, mean that if Mr Mudryk's sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no ADRVs would have resulted. "Further to that development and to other circumstances of the case, The FA and Mr Mudryk have now - with the agreement of WADA - resolved the appeal proceedings in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the World Anti-Doping Code and Regulation 90 of the 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations. As a part of the agreement, Mr Mudryk accepted that he had committed the Anti-Doping Rule Violations charged and acceded to a period of ineligibility equal to the time served at the date of the agreement. Mr Mudryk is no longer ineligible and may return to competition with immediate effect."

A Chelsea statement added: "Chelsea FC acknowledges today's announcement by The Football Association confirming the resolution of the anti-doping proceedings involving Mykhailo Mudryk.

‌



"From the outset, this has been an extremely difficult period for Misha, both professionally and personally, and we are pleased that the matter has now reached a conclusion which allows him to return to football with immediate effect.

View 2 Images Mudryk signed for Chelsea from Shakhtar Donetsk in 2023 (Image: Getty Images)

"We have always supported Misha throughout this process while fully respecting the integrity of the anti-doping system and the legal process.

‌



"We welcome the acknowledgement that advances in the applicable scientific reporting standards for more reliable testing mean that, had Misha's sample been analysed under today's technical requirements, it would not have been reported as a positive test and no anti-doping rule violation would have resulted. That is an important part of the context surrounding the agreed resolution and allows everyone involved to move forward.

"Misha has consistently maintained that he never knowingly or intentionally used a prohibited substance and did not know how traces of the substance entered his system. Throughout this process he has conducted himself professionally and with resilience during what has undoubtedly been one of the most challenging periods of his career.

"We know how much this opportunity to return means to him. Our focus now is on supporting Misha’s reintegration into the squad and helping him resume his career.

‌



"Chelsea FC remains fully committed to the highest standards of sporting integrity and compliance with all anti-doping regulations. Everyone at the Club now looks forward to helping Misha return to full fitness, back into the squad and back onto the pitch."

Mudryk, 25, joined Chelsea for £62 million in January 2023 from Shakhtar Donetsk, the Blues having beaten Premier League rivals Arsenal to his signature. He endured a tough debut campaign, failing to score in 17 appearances. Things were slightly better the following campaign, as Mudryk netted seven times in 41 appearances, with a further three goals the next season before being banned.

Mudryk signed a eight-and-a-half year deal with Chelsea, that deal set to run until 2031. He is now expected to rejoin the Chelsea squad in Hong Kong.

Sports.title: 'Lighten up!' - Hull responds to caddie prank criticism during major push
Sports.content:
Charley Hull insists she 'does not care' about criticism over her pre-major caddie prank and overcame limited sleep to remain firmly in AIG Women's Open title contention.

Hull followed an opening-round 69 with a level-par 71 on Friday morning at Royal Lytham & St Annes, mixing three birdies with as many bogeys to head into the weekend on two under and in contention in the final major of the year.

She faced scrutiny on social media after admitting pre-tournament that she tricked her caddie Adam Woodward into thinking he'd won £100,000 on a scratchcard, capturing the moment on camera after purchasing the fake ticket in a Blackpool joke shop.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hull reveals the hilarious scratchcard prank she pulled on her caddie Adam Woodward ahead of the AIG Women's Open.

Hull insists she was unaffected by the negative comments and that her caddie embraced the 'banter', with the world No 7 now fully focused on making a weekend charge and challenging for an elusive major victory.

"I don't think people understand mine and Adsy's [Woodward, caddie] relationship," Hull said post-round. "We're very, very close. He's like a big brother to me. He is one of my best friends.

"He's always taking the mickey out of me. He thought the joke was brilliant himself - he was showing everybody about it and he was laughing hard about it. Then when you hear comments, so many people saying how bad it is, I'm like 'just lighten up'.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hull holed a bunker shot for birdie at the 17th hole to close on clubhouse leader Shiho Kuwaki

"I don't care if you don't get my humour - my friends get my humour and that's why they're my friends. I wouldn't do it to a random person that I knew wouldn't take it very well.

"We all know Adsy is the king of pranks. The amount of pranks he and his caddie mates are just way worse than that, and he just finds it hilarious. He's pretty chill and people need to chill out about that. Adsy is loving the attention from it!

"He texted me last night saying this has been one of the funniest weeks ever because of that prank, so people need to stop writing bad comments and stuff because they need to lighten up. If you got something bad to say about it, I don't care!"

Image: Charley Hull with caddie Adam Woodward during the AIG Women's Open

When asked how Hull responds to negative comments, she added: "They actually make me want to do better because I think we live in a world where you can't do anything wrong these days, and then it stops people from living the life they want to.

"I don't care - I just live me. Our household has a lot of banter and are always taking the mickey out of each other. It's just the way I've been brought up, and I think people just need to be a bit more tough-skinned.

"I think you put yourself in the limelight so you would be silly to think there will not be comments like that. I think you see some people saying I really struggle from these comments and they're almost looking for sympathy.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking ahead of the tournament, Hull claims she doesn't see Nelly Korda as her rival due to the fact she's yet to lift a major title

"I'm just like 'you're in such a good position in life. There are people way worse off in life and you're moaning about what people are saying about you'. I just think grow a pair of balls and just forget about it, do you know what I mean?

"If that's the worst thing in life, people saying bad stuff about you, you really have not got life that bad."

Hull admitted she only had around three hours' sleep ahead of her second round, with the Englishman - a five-time major runner-up who has finished second twice in the last three years at this event - ready for the challenge ahead.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hull holed a bunker shot for birdie at the 17th hole to close on clubhouse leader Shiho Kuwaki

"Really looking forward to it," Hull said. "It's going to be loads of fun. I feel like now my nerves have settled down. My back was actually playing up for me a little bit today, a little bit sore, that's why I think I wasn't getting through the ball how I wanted to.

"Not too far going into the weekend - better than I was last year!"

Sports.title: Chelsea handed £10m fine and suspended transfer ban
Sports.content:
Chelsea have been fined £10m and given a suspended two-window transfer ban by an independent appeal board after admitting breaches of Football Association agent rules, the FA has announced.

An earlier independent commission had imposed a suspended six-point deduction, which was set aside and the suspended transfer ban imposed in its place.

The FA confirmed the imposition of sanctions on the west London club on Friday, who admitted to a total of 74 breaches of FA regulations covering agents, working with intermediaries and third-party investment in players.

The club's new owners self-reported the breaches to the football authorities in May 2022, when they were in the process of buying the club from Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich.

The transfers which raised potential concerns during the takeover process are believed to include deals for players such as Eden Hazard, Samuel Eto'o and Willian. There is no suggestion of any wrongdoing on the part of those players.

The six-point deduction, suspended until June 30 2027, was imposed by the independent commission which initially heard the case but the club appealed against that. An appeal board instead replaced the points penalty with the suspended two-window transfer ban.

The £10m fine imposed by the Regulatory Commission was not subject to appeal and the full amount will be invested into grassroots football.

Chelsea have previously entered sanction settlements in regard to this matter with the Premier League and UEFA.

A club statement read: "Chelsea Football Club is pleased to confirm that a final decision has been reached by The FA's judicial bodies in relation to historical regulatory matters that were self-reported by the club.

"In 2022, the club self-reported potential historical rule breaches to all applicable regulators. Following that report, it has worked openly and transparently with all regulators, including voluntarily and proactively disclosing many thousands of documents.

Image: The payments were made under former Chelsea owner Roman Abramovich

"As previously announced, settlement agreements have been entered into with UEFA and the Premier League concerning the same self-reported regulatory matters and topics that have been addressed before. The club is pleased to confirm that, now The FA process has concluded, this brings all regulatory proceedings against the club to a close.

"We are grateful to UEFA, the Premier League and The FA for their engagement with the club throughout these processes."

Earlier this year, Chelsea were handed the Premier League's biggest fine along with a one-year transfer ban, suspended for two years. The total fine of £10.75m related to secret payments made to agents worth £47.5m between 2011 and 2018, when Roman Abramovich was owner, and breaches of rules around registering youth players.

The total fine was going to be £20m but it was halved because the Blues self-reported and co-operated with the investigation.

The Premier League report named a number of transfers related to the secret payments, including deals for Hazard, Eto'o, Willian, Ramires, David Luiz, Andre Schurrle and Nemanja Matic. The names of four players were redacted in the report.

Image: Former Chelsea forward Eden Hazard was among the players mentioned in various offences, although there is no indication of wrongdoing from the player himself

Clubs must provide the FA and Premier League accurate financial information every year. The same applies for UEFA and clubs playing in their competition.

Chelsea were fined £8.64m by UEFA in July 2023 for incomplete financial reporting by the previous owners in 2018 and 2019. At least six suspect payments to offshore companies connected to transfers were identified.

'Some fans may be thinking Chelsea have got off lightly'

Analysis from Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol:

"On one hand, it's not good news for Chelsea because they've been hit with a fine and a suspended transfer ban, but I imagine a lot of people who are not Chelsea supporters will be thinking 'Chelsea have got off lightly, they really should have got a points deduction'.

"I'm sure fans of clubs who have been hit with points deductions in the past will be saying 'why did we get real punishments that affected our seasons when Chelsea are just getting a financial penalty which their owners can afford to pay?'

"Chelsea have been fined three times for offences that came to light and were reported by the new owners.

"Having said that, when you read stories and opinion on this, people feel Chelsea have got off lightly, but I'm sure their supporters and owners would say 'we got fined by UEFA, the Premier League and the FA. We've been punished three times for the same offences that we didn't commit. It was the previous ownership'."

Sports.title: Chelsea's Mudryk cleared to play after doping ban resolved
Sports.content:
Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk has been cleared to return to play after his doping ban was resolved.

The 25-year-old has not played competitively since November 2024 after he was suspended for four years for failing a drug test, which revealed the presence of a low concentration of meldonium, a prohibited substance, two years ago.

Mudryk filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) while changes to World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) procedures in the interim mean that had his failed test produced the same result now, charges would not have been brought.

The FA said: "Changes have been made… which, while not retroactive, mean that if Mr Mudryk's sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no anti-doping rule violations would have resulted.

"Further to that development and to other circumstances of the case, the FA and Mr Mudryk have now - with the agreement of WADA - resolved the appeal proceedings.

"As a part of the agreement, Mr Mudryk accepted that he had committed the ADRVs (Anti-Doping Rule Violations) charged and acceded to a period of ineligibility equal to the time served at the date of the agreement.

"Mr Mudryk is no longer ineligible and may return to competition with immediate effect."

That is an important part of the context surrounding the agreed resolution and allows everyone involved to move forward."

The Ukraine international also released a statement in which he said his two years away from football have "been the most difficult period of my career" and that he was "grateful" to be able to return.

Mudryk's charity shop work during ban - but will he play for Blues this season?

Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol:

Mudryk believed his sample, which tested positive for heart drug meldonium, was contaminated when he was on international duty with Ukraine in October 2024.

He tested positive during a period when Ukraine played in Albania and Georgia in November 2024 before then being provisionally suspended by the FA a month later.

Mudryk has always maintained his innocence and had been keeping fit by working with his own personal trainers away from Chelsea's Cobham training ground.

In fact, he was recently spotted working in a charity shop in London. Mudryk has not been allowed to train at Chelsea's Cobham training ground.

It now remains to be seen whether Mudryk will be part of Xabi Alonso's squad this season.

Chelsea have the option of sending him on loan to regain full match fitness.

Sports.title: F1 contracts: How long is each driver signed up for?
Sports.content:
A look at how long each Formula 1 driver's contract is believed to be, as it stands in 2026, amid the potential for some key moves heading into the 2027 season.

McLaren

Lando Norris - 2027

Lando Norris agreed to an extension shortly before the start of the 2024 F1 season on a "multi-year" extension to his previous deal, which had been set to expire in 2025.

This means reigning world champion Norris is tied to McLaren until at least the end of 2027.

Oscar Piastri - 2028

Oscar Piastri signed a new multi-year contract extension ahead of the 2025 F1 season that will keep him at McLaren until the end of 2028.

Barring an intra-team fallout or significant drop in performance, it's hard to see Norris or Piastri moving teams next year.

Mercedes

George Russell - 2027

Officially, Mercedes announced George Russell only for 2026 after speculation throughout last summer.

But, Sky Sports News understands Russell signed a multi-year contract so will be with Mercedes until at least the end of 2027.

Kimi Antonelli - 2026

Mercedes confirmed Kimi Antonelli will remain for 2026 at the same time as their October announcement regarding Russell's future.

Given Antonelli is in the early stages of his F1 career, having been on Mercedes' books since the age of 12, and they continue to view him as a star of the future despite challenges in his rookie season, it would be surprising if the Italian's overarching deal wasn't longer-term with accompanying options around the F1 seat.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli superbly won the 2026 Monaco Grand Prix

Red Bull

Max Verstappen - 2028

Max Verstappen signed a long-term deal back in March 2022 to stay at Red Bull until the end of 2028. However, there are understood to be performance clauses in Verstappen's contract that can see him leave the team, which was highlighted in 2024 during the height of inapproiate behaviour allegations made against Christian Horner, which were dismissed later that year.

Verstappen has consistently stated he wants to be able to compete for wins, so if Red Bull cannot provide him that, and he does not enjoy the new 2026 cars, there will inevitably be question marks surrounding his future.

Isack Hadjar - 2026

Isack Hadjar will be the seventh driver in the last eight years to try their hand at being Verstappen's team-mate at Red Bull following his impressive rookie campaign at Racing Bulls.

Hadjar's future will be largely dictated around how close he is to Verstappen, regardless of how strong the RB22 is.

Ferrari

Charles Leclerc - 2028

Charles Leclerc penned his latest Ferrari deal in June 2026. As with his previous agreement, announced in January 2024, the team did not publicly comment on the length of his contract, simply saying that it secured Leclerc's future at Maranello "for the coming seasons".

That would take Leclerc up to at least the end of 2028, while there may also be options beyond that to extend further too.

Lewis Hamilton - 2027

Lewis Hamilton's shock announcement in February 2024 to join Ferrari in 2025 was one of the biggest F1 transfer deals in the sport's history.

Ferrari announced the move as a multi-year deal. Hamilton provided more clarity on the precise length of that term when he confirmed at the 2026 Canadian Grand Prix that he also had a contract in place for at least 2027, which would be his third year at the team. Sky Sports F1 understands Hamilton also holds a unilateral option for 2028 too.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton claimed his first win in red at the 2026 Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix

Williams

Alex Albon - 2026

Alex Albon agreed a new multi-year contract extension Mary 2024, so is confirmed at Williams until the end of this year.

Albon joined Williams in 2022 and stood firm in his first season as Carlos Sainz's team-mate in 2025, so another strong campaign could see him sign a new contract for 2027 and beyond.

Carlos Sainz - 2026

Sainz signed a two-year Williams contract which began in 2025 with "options to extend" beyond 2026.

Given the high stock of Sainz, Williams will be keen to keep the Spaniard but if the car is uncompetitive, could Sainz look elsewhere?

Racing Bulls

Liam Lawson - 2026

Liam Lawson will look to establish himself as the lead driver at Racing Bulls against rookie Arvid Lindblad and should he really impress Red Bull, it should not be ruled out about the possibility of him being in contention to return to the main team.

If that's not possible, Lawson may talk to other teams to secure a spot on the 2027 grid, but he must first deliver some strong results.

Arvid Lindblad - 2026

British teenager Lindblad is the only rookie on the 2026 grid after impressing Red Bull in his three practice outings last year, finishing sixth in first practice in Mexico City.

The 18-year-old just needs to ensure he does not make any big mistakes and if can match, or beat, team-mate Lawson, at the very least he will have a second season at Racing Bulls.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch as F1 drivers reunite to take their class of 2026 season photo

Aston Martin

Fernando Alonso - 2026

Fernando Alonso agreed a contract extension in April 2024 to remain with Aston Martin until at least the end of the 2026 F1 season.

Alonso is the oldest driver on the grid and will turn 45 later this year, which would make him the first driver to compete in Formula 1 at that age since Graham Hill in 1975.

Aston Martin appear to be on the backfoot, so there will naturally be questions about whether Alonso will retire at the end of this season.

Lance Stroll - 2026

Lance Stroll is the only driver in the field whose contract details are largely unknown, partly because he is the son of team owner Lawrence Stroll, and appears to have a seat for as long as his father remains in that position.

Stroll has been outperformed by Alonso during their three seasons together but Aston Martin formally announced in June 2024 that the Canadian has a deal for "2025 and beyond".

Haas

Oliver Bearman - 2026

Oliver Bearman's first full F1 campaign in 2025 saw a mixture of high-profile mistakes and lightning speed - with the latter aspect leading to speculation over whether he could replace Hamilton at Ferrari in the future.

Haas are unlikely to be front-runners in F1 any time soon, so at 20 years old, Bearman could be a key name in the driver market this season, should he impress on the track.

Esteban Ocon - 2026

Esteban Ocon's stock has fallen slightly over the last two years after a disappointing end to his time at Alpine in 2024 and being outperformed by Bearman at Haas in 2025.

Ocon will aim to get on top of Bearman in the inter-team battle, which could be important given both drivers have not been confirmed for 2027.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oliver Bearman discusses his ambition to one day be in a Ferrari seat, but admits he's 'just getting started' with Haas

Audi

Nico Hulkenberg - 2026

Nico Hulkenberg signed a multi-year contract when he joined Sauber, which is now Audi, in 2025 which means he does not necessarily have a seat beyond this season.

Hulkenberg still seems to enjoy F1 and has not shown any signs of retiring despite being a father and 38 years old.

Gabriel Bortoleto - 2026

Gabriel Bortoleto perhaps did not hit the heights many expected after winning the F3 and F2 titles in his rookie seasons on his way to F1.

Bortoleto improved as 2025 went on and is still one of the best young talents on the grid, so it will be in Audi's best interests to keep the 21-year-old.

Alpine

Pierre Gasly - 2028

Pierre Gasly announced a new contract last September to stay at Alpine until at least the end of 2028, having joined the team in 2023.

Gasly has established himself as the lead driver at Alpine and a more competitive car this year could see him cause some surprise results when the top teams trip up.

Franco Colapinto - 2026

Franco Colapinto replaced Jack Doohan just six rounds into the 2025 season and recovered from a shaky start to his Alpine career to earn a seat for this season.

The Argentine will need to find another step in performance to remain with the team for 2027 but currently has the backing of Alpine executive advisor Flavio Briatore.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Craig Slater sits down with Franco Colapinto to discuss his new contract at Alpine

Cadillac

Sergio Perez - 2027

Sergio Perez returns to F1 this year with newcomers Cadillac after a season out of the sport and will be with the American outfit for at least two seasons.

Although Perez was only confirmed for 2026, Sky Sports News understands he signed a multi-year deal.

Valtteri Bottas - 2027

Valtteri Bottas is also understood to have agreed a multi-year contract that will see him be with Cadillac until at least the end of 2027.

Just like Perez, he spent 2025 on the sidelines but will be hoping to add a few more highlights to his F1 career.

Sports.title: 'I want it so badly!' - Emotional Tamburlini faces nervous Solheim wait
Sports.content:
An emotional Chiara Tamburlini faces a nervous wait to see if she has qualified for Team Europe’s Solheim Cup side after missing the cut at the AIG Women’s Open.

Tamburlini came into the final women's major of the year second in the Ladies European Tour's Solheim Cup points list, with the top two in those standings after this week securing their spot in Anna Nordqvist's side.

The Swiss player arrived at Royal Lytham & St Annes with a slender 1.1-point lead over Helen Briem, with Tamburlini posting a four-bogey finish to her opening-round 75 and confirming her early exit with a three-over 74 on Friday morning.

Briem and France's Agathe Laisne also missed the cut to end their automatic qualification hopes, but Tamburlini is still left relying on other players' performances over the weekend to see whether she will make her Solheim Cup debut.
